definition_zh: 消费者；用户；消耗者；（生态学中的）取食者
definition_en: a person who buys and uses goods and services, or more broadly any person, organism or program that uses something up
core_image: 超市收银台前，购物篮里的东西一件件被放上传送带，人离开时篮子已经空了
scene: 收银台前的队伍缓慢前移，篮里的东西被一件件放上传送带，人走时篮子空了。The average consumer now spends more on services than on manufactured goods.
sceneCN: 收银台前的顾客把商品逐件放上传送带，付款后篮子空掉；句中的 consumer 指「为自用而购买商品或服务的人」（第 1 个义项：处在链条末端、最终购买并使用的人，而非转售者）。图中可辨识物件：收银台、传送带、购物篮、价签、付款屏幕。

derivatives.zh: 消费主义者；消费主义的

senses.title: A person who buys for personal use
senses.titleCN: 为自己使用而购买商品与服务的人
senses.definition: a person who buys goods or services for personal needs rather than for resale or production
senses.definitionCN: 为自身需要而非转售或生产而购买商品或服务的人
senses.example: The average consumer now spends more on services than on manufactured goods.
senses.exampleCN: 如今普通消费者在服务上的花费超过在制成品上的花费。
senses.why: The economic sense grows straight out of the verb: the one who consumes stands at the end of the chain and uses the good up.
senses.whyCN: 经济义直接从动词生长出来：处在链条末端、把商品用掉的人，就是消费者。

senses.title: The user of a utility or public service
senses.titleCN: 公共设施或公共服务的用户
senses.definition: a household or individual that uses electricity, water, transport or another service supplied by a utility
senses.definitionCN: 使用电力、供水、交通等公共机构所提供服务的家庭或个人
senses.example: Domestic consumers pay a lower tariff than factories do.
senses.exampleCN: 居民用户比工厂支付更低的费率。
senses.why: Once buying is separated from using, anyone who draws on a supply counts as a consumer of it, even without a shop.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把「购买」与「使用」分开，凡从某种供应中取用的人就算它的消费者，即使没有商店也成立。

senses.title: An organism that feeds on others
senses.titleCN: 生态学中以其他生物为食的取食者
senses.definition: an organism that obtains energy by eating other organisms rather than by making its own food
senses.definitionCN: 靠吃其他生物获取能量，而非自行制造养分的生物
senses.example: In a pond, small fish act as consumers of the algae.
senses.exampleCN: 在池塘里，小鱼充当藻类的取食者。
senses.why: Ecology borrowed the word because eating is the clearest case of using up what another organism has built.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用这个词，因为「吃」正是把别的生物造出的东西用掉的最明显例子。

senses.title: A heavy user of a shared resource
senses.titleCN: 大量消耗共用资源的人或群体
senses.definition: a person, group or country that draws heavily on a shared resource such as fuel, water or land
senses.definitionCN: 大量取用燃料、水、土地等共用资源的个人、群体或国家
senses.example: Rich nations are heavy consumers of fossil fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 富裕国家是化石燃料的大量消耗者。
senses.why: Here the object consumed is no longer a product on a shelf but a stock that everyone shares, so the word turns into a criticism.
senses.whyCN: 这里被消耗的不再是货架上的商品，而是众人共享的存量，于是这个词带上了批评意味。

senses.title: The household side in economic statistics
senses.titleCN: 经济统计中的居民消费一方
senses.definition: the category of households and individuals whose spending is measured in national accounts
senses.definitionCN: 国民经济核算中加以计量的家庭与个人支出类别
senses.example: Consumer spending accounts for roughly two thirds of the economy.
senses.exampleCN: 消费者支出约占经济总量的三分之二。
senses.why: Statistics need a label for one side of the ledger, and the word shifts from a person to an aggregate of persons.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要一个标签来指账目的一侧，于是这个词从「一个人」转为「一群人的加总」。

senses.title: A program that requests data
senses.titleCN: 计算机中请求数据或服务的一方
senses.definition: a program or device that requests data or a service from another program, called the provider
senses.definitionCN: 向另一个程序（提供方）请求数据或服务的程序或设备
senses.example: The app is a consumer of the weather service, not its owner.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用是天气服务的使用方，而不是它的所有者。
senses.why: Computing keeps the shape of the old sense: one side produces, the other takes and uses, and the taker is named the consumer.
senses.whyCN: 计算机保留了旧义的结构：一方生产，另一方取用，取用的一方被称为消费方。

senses.title: A buyer shaped by marketing
senses.titleCN: 被广告与营销左右选择的购买者
senses.definition: a member of the public seen as someone whose choices can be guided by advertising and packaging
senses.definitionCN: 被视为其选择可被广告与包装引导的公众成员
senses.example: Regulators argued that the consumer deserves clearer labels on packaged food.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者主张，消费者应当得到更清晰的包装食品标签。
senses.why: The same person is now viewed from the seller's side, as a target to be informed or persuaded, which is why the word appears in rules and campaigns.
senses.whyCN: 同一个人现在从卖方视角被看待，成了要被告知或说服的对象，因此这个词常出现在法规与宣传中。

senses.title: Anything that uses what another produces
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：消耗他人产出的一方
senses.definition: any entity that uses up what another entity produces, whether goods, evidence or attention
senses.definitionCN: 消耗另一实体所生产之物的任何主体，无论那是商品、证据还是注意力
senses.example: A good theory is a consumer of evidence rather than a substitute for it.
senses.exampleCN: 好的理论是证据的使用者，而不是证据的替代品。
senses.why: Stripped of shops and organisms, the word keeps only its structural role: the receiving end of a supply.
senses.whyCN: 剥去商店与生物的外壳，这个词只剩下结构性的角色：一份供应所流向的接收端。

intro.en: Consumer is the agent noun of consume, which came through Old French from Latin consumere, built on com- 'thoroughly' and sumere 'to take up'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: consumer 是动词 consume 的施动名词；consume 经古法语来自拉丁语 consumere，该词由表「彻底」的前缀与 sumere「取、拿」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Sumere meant 'to take up, take on', made of sub- 'under' and emere 'to take, buy'. The deeper origin of emere is not established.
items.cn: sumere 意为「拿起、承担」，由表「在下」的前缀加 emere「取、买」构成；emere 的更深来源未得到证明。

items.en: Com- 'thoroughly' plus sumere produced consumere, 'to take wholly, use up, waste or destroy'.
items.cn: 表「彻底」的前缀加 sumere 构成 consumere，意为「整个取走、用尽、耗费」，也可指毁掉。

items.en: Old French consumer carried the verb into English in the fourteenth century with the sense 'to use up, wear away'.
items.cn: 古法语 consumer 在十四世纪把这个动词带入英语，义为「用光、耗损」。

items.en: The person noun appears in the sixteenth century, at first meaning someone who squanders or wastes; the neutral buyer sense belongs to the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 指人的名词在十六世纪出现，最初指挥霍、浪费的人；中性的购买者义要到十八世纪才确立。

items.en: National accounts turned the word into a statistical category in the twentieth century, while ecology used it for the eater in a food chain and computing for the program that requests data.
items.cn: 国民经济核算在二十世纪把它变成统计类别；生态学用它指食物链中的取食者；计算机领域用它指请求数据的程序。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first date of the neutral economic sense is not settled, and the origin of emere before Latin is unknown, so any root offered for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：中性经济义的确切首见年代没有定论；emere 在拉丁语之前的来源不明，凡为其给出的词根均属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms built on the same consuming verb, each with a different grammatical job; group two holds words for people who acquire or operate things, each stressing a different part of the transaction.
note.cn: 第一组同出「消耗」这一动词，只是句法功能不同；第二组都指获得或使用某物的人，但各自强调交易中的不同环节。

entries.definition: The verb for using something up; the person noun cannot take its place in a sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 表示用光的动词；指人的名词不能取代它在句中的位置。

entries.definition: Names the act or the quantity used; it is not a person, so it cannot be called a careful consumer.
entries.definitionCN: 指行为或用量，不是指人，因此不能说某人是谨慎的消费量。

entries.definition: Either an excessive attachment to buying or the movement that defends buyers; it is not the buyer himself.
entries.definitionCN: 或指对购物的过度热衷，或指维护买方的运动；它并不指买方本人。

entries.definition: An adjective, and a noun for an item that wears out in use, such as ink or paper.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，也可作名词，指使用中会耗尽的东西，如墨水或纸张。

entries.definition: Someone who buys from a particular shop or company; the link is with the seller, not with using the goods up.
entries.definitionCN: 从某家商店或公司购买的人；其联系在卖方，而不在商品是否被用掉。

entries.definition: Someone who operates a product or service; the word says nothing about payment or ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 操作某产品或服务的人；这个词不涉及付款或所有权。

entries.definition: The plain word for the person who pays; in business it can also mean the person who purchases for a company.
entries.definitionCN: 指付款者的普通词；在商业中也可指为公司采购的人。

entries.definition: A formal counterpart of buyer, common in contracts and records.
entries.definitionCN: buyer 的正式对应词，常见于合同与档案。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations here are the real Latin steps, the real word family and the real fixed phrases, not invented sound-alikes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取自这个词真实的拉丁语演变、真实词族与真实固定搭配，而非编造的同音联想。

normal.en: The prefix means 'thoroughly': the taking is complete, so what is taken is used up.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「彻底」：取的动作做到底，被取之物也就被用尽了。

normal.en: The family runs consume, consumer, consumption, consumerism, consumable.
normal.cn: 词族包括 consume、consumer、consumption、consumerism、consumable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the economic sense: consumer goods, consumer spending, consumer confidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出经济义：消费品、消费者支出、消费者信心。

normal.en: Ecology pairs consumer with producer, the eater with the maker.
normal.cn: 生态学把消费者与生产者配对，取食者与制造者相对。

normal.en: Computing pairs consumer with provider: one asks for data, the other supplies it.
normal.cn: 计算机领域把消费方与提供方配对：一方请求数据，另一方供给。

abstract.en: Picture a basket that starts full at the checkout and is empty by the time it reaches the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象一只篮子，在收银台时是满的，到厨房时已经空了。

abstract.en: Picture a river that everybody drinks from but nobody pays to keep clean.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河，人人都从中取水，却没人出钱维护它的清洁。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that gives light only because another room keeps generating power.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯能亮，只因为另一间屋子一直在发电。

examples.en: Consumer prices rose more slowly than wages last year.
examples.cn: 去年消费品价格的上涨慢于工资的上涨。

examples.en: Energy consumers were asked to cut use during the cold snap.
examples.cn: 严寒期间，能源用户被要求削减用量。

examples.en: The study treats the household as both producer and consumer of care.
examples.cn: 这项研究把家庭同时视为照护的生产者与消费者。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「看见（con）就买，买了就用光（sum）」——掏钱并把东西用掉的人，就是消费者

root: 拉丁语 consumere（用尽、耗尽）＝表「彻底」的前缀＋sumere（取、拿，由 sub-「在下」＋emere「取、买」构成）；emere 更深来源不确定。英语 consumer 为 consume 的施动名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one position: the end of a supply chain where something is taken and used up, filled first by a shopper, then by a utility user, an organism, a drain on resources, a statistical category, a requesting program and finally any receiving side at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个位置展开：供应链末端那个「取走并用掉」的位置；先由购物者占据，再由设施用户、生物、资源消耗者、统计类别、请求数据的程序占据，最后泛指任何接收的一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a basket that is full at the checkout and empty at home.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只在收银台装满、到家已空的篮子。

branches.en: BUYER: the shopper is the first holder of the role, seen once from his own side and once from the seller's.
branches.cn: 购买者：购物者最先占据这个角色，一次从自身视角看，一次从卖方视角看。

branches.en: UTILITY USER: paying for a service and using it are separated, so the role passes to any household drawing on a supply.
branches.cn: 设施用户：付费与使用被分开，角色就传给任何从供应中取用的家庭。

branches.en: DRAIN ON A SUPPLY: an organism eats others, and a country draws down a shared stock; both consume what is not theirs alone.
branches.cn: 供应的消耗方：生物吃别的生物，国家耗用共享存量；两者都在消耗并非独属自己的东西。

branches.en: STATISTICAL CATEGORY: many persons become one line in the accounts, so the role turns into an aggregate.
branches.cn: 统计类别：许多人合成账目上的一行，角色于是变成一种加总。

branches.en: STRUCTURAL ROLE: a program asks a provider for data, and any receiver of a supply repeats the same shape.
branches.cn: 结构角色：程序向提供方请求数据，任何供应的接收方都重复同一结构。

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin verb and an English agent suffix, and each piece still works on its own in other words.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁动词与一个英语施动后缀构成，每一部分在其他词里仍能独立起作用。

latinIntro.en: Latin sumere and its compound consumere supply the root; the English suffix marks the person who performs the action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sumere 及其复合形式 consumere 提供词根；英语后缀标出执行动作的人。

items.example: The prefix gives the act a sense of completion.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀赋予动作一种「做到底」的意味。

items.example: The root names the act of taking something.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根点明「取走某物」的动作。

items.example: Sumere adds the idea of lifting something to oneself.
items.exampleCN: sumere 增添了「把东西拿到自己这边」的意思。

items.example: The compound names taking something until nothing is left.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词指取用到一点也不剩。

items.meaning: to use up, eat or drink
items.example: Factories consume large amounts of power.
items.exampleCN: 工厂消耗大量电力。

items.example: The consumer pays the final price.
items.exampleCN: 消费者支付最终价格。

items.example: Consumption of coal fell again.
items.exampleCN: 煤炭消耗量再次下降。

items.meaningCN: 以购买为中心的制度或运动
items.example: Consumerism reshaped the high street.
items.exampleCN: 消费主义重塑了商业街。

items.example: Ink and paper are consumable supplies.
items.exampleCN: 墨水与纸张属于消耗品。

derivatives.zh: 消费主义者；消费主义的

definition_zh: 支出；开支；花费（尤指机构或政府的总支出）
definition_en: the total amount of money spent, especially by a government, company or household over a period
core_image: 一只钱袋被打开，硬币按类别分堆倒出，堆与堆之间高低不同
scene: 月底的账本摊在桌上，各类开销被分堆相加，总数比预想的更沉。Public expenditure on health rose faster than spending on roads.
sceneCN: 账本上各类开销分堆相加，总额超出预想；句中的 expenditure 指「政府或机构在一段时期内的总支出」（第 1 个义项：按期间汇总的支出总额）。图中可辨识物件：摊开的账本、分堆的硬币、计算器、笔、预算表。

senses.title: Total money spent over a period
senses.titleCN: 一段时期内的支出总额
senses.definition: the total sum of money that a government, company or household spends during a stated period
senses.definitionCN: 政府、公司或家庭在特定期间花掉的钱的总和
senses.example: Public expenditure on health rose faster than spending on roads.
senses.exampleCN: 公共卫生支出比道路支出增长得更快。
senses.why: The noun names the whole outflow rather than one bill, which is why it usually appears with a period or an institution.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指整个流出量而不是一笔账单，因此通常与时间段或机构连用。

senses.title: The act of paying money out
senses.definition: the act or practice of paying money out, especially in a planned or measured way
senses.definitionCN: 付出钱款的行为或做法，尤指有计划的、有计量的付出
senses.example: Careful expenditure kept the project within its budget.
senses.exampleCN: 谨慎的开支使项目保持在预算之内。
senses.why: English allows an action noun to stand beside the amount noun, so the same word names both the spending and what is spent.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许动作名词与数量名词并存，于是同一个词既指花钱这件事，也指花掉的钱。

senses.title: One recorded item of spending
senses.definition: a particular sum paid out for a stated purpose and recorded as a single entry
senses.definitionCN: 为特定用途付出、并作为单独一笔记录下来的款项
senses.example: The auditor questioned an expenditure on outside consultants.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员质疑了一笔支付给外部顾问的支出。
senses.why: Once accounts are kept line by line, the mass of spending is cut into countable pieces and each piece takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 账目一旦逐行记录，整块支出就被切成可数的片段，每个片段都用同一个名称。

senses.title: Household spending on consumption
senses.definition: the money a household lays out on goods and services in ordinary living
senses.definitionCN: 家庭为日常生活中的商品与服务所付出的钱
senses.example: Household expenditure fell sharply after the fuel price rose.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料价格上涨后，家庭支出大幅下降。
senses.why: Economics needs to separate the household sector from the government sector, so the word is paired with the spending unit.
senses.whyCN: 经济学需要把家庭部门与政府部门分开，因此这个词常与支出单位搭配。

senses.title: Spending on long-lived assets
senses.titleCN: 用于长期资产的资本支出
senses.definition: money spent on buildings, machines or other assets expected to be used for years
senses.definitionCN: 用于建筑、机器或其他预期使用多年的资产的钱
senses.example: The firm's capital expenditure went into new turbines.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司的资本支出投向了新的涡轮机。
senses.why: Accounting distinguishes money that keeps running from money that is gone, and the lasting kind gets a fixed phrase of its own.
senses.whyCN: 会计要区分「能持续运转的钱」与「已经花掉的钱」，能持续的那一类便有了自己的固定搭配。

senses.title: Government spending on services
senses.titleCN: 政府用于公共服务的开支
senses.definition: the money a state spends on schools, hospitals, defence and other public services
senses.definitionCN: 国家用于学校、医院、国防及其他公共服务的钱
senses.example: Rising expenditure on pensions dominated the budget debate.
senses.exampleCN: 养老金支出的上升主导了预算辩论。
senses.why: Because public budgets are debated as totals, the word became the standard label for what a state lays out.
senses.whyCN: 由于公共预算以总额形式被辩论，这个词就成了国家花钱的标准说法。

senses.title: Energy or effort used up
senses.titleCN: 体力、精力或能量的消耗量
senses.definition: the amount of energy, time or effort that an activity uses up
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动所消耗的能量、时间或精力总量
senses.example: Running uphill involves a much higher expenditure of energy.
senses.exampleCN: 上坡跑涉及高得多的能量消耗。
senses.why: The older sense of paying out extends naturally to any reserve that is drawn down, money being only one such reserve.
senses.whyCN: 「付出」的旧义自然延伸到任何被取用的储备，钱只是其中一种储备。

senses.title: Abstract outlay paid for later
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：为日后收益先付出的代价
senses.definition: any cost paid in advance, in money, patience or risk, in order to obtain something later
senses.definitionCN: 为日后获得某物而预先付出的任何代价，可以是金钱、耐心或风险
senses.example: The expedition's success was bought with an expenditure of patience rather than money.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考察的成功是用耐心而非金钱的付出换来的。
senses.why: At its most general the word means a deliberate laying out of something valuable, whatever currency is used.
senses.whyCN: 在最一般的层面上，这个词指有意把有价值之物拿出去，无论用的是哪种「货币」。

intro.en: Expenditure is an English noun built on the Latin verb expendere 'to weigh out, pay out', whose root pendere meant 'to hang' and hence 'to weigh'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expenditure 是英语中构成的名词，基础是拉丁动词 expendere「称出、付出」，其词根 pendere 意为「悬挂」，引申为「称量」。年代为约数。

items.en: Pendere meant 'to hang' and, because money was weighed, 'to weigh out and pay'. The common link to a root meaning 'to stretch or spin' is a reconstruction.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂」，又因钱要称量而指「称出、支付」。常被引用的、与表示「拉伸或纺织」的词根的联系属于重构形式。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pendere produced expendere, 'to weigh out, pay out, spend'.
items.cn: 表「向外」的前缀加 pendere 构成 expendere，意为「称出、付出、花费」。

items.en: The feminine past participle became the noun expensa, 'money paid out', a familiar word in medieval account books.
items.cn: 其阴性过去分词转为名词 expensa，意为「付出的钱」，是中世纪账簿中的常用词。

items.en: The shortened form passed through Old French as espense and entered English in the thirteenth century as expense.
items.cn: 缩短后的形式经古法语 espense 在十三世纪进入英语，成为 expense。

items.en: Expenditure was formed inside English from expend plus a suffix of Latin origin meaning an act or its result, first in the eighteenth century, and it took over the collective sense that expense had held.
items.cn: expenditure 是在英语内部由 expend 加一个源自拉丁语、表示行为或结果的后缀构成，最早见于十八世纪，并接过了 expense 原先承担的「总额」义。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of expenditure is not pinned down beyond the eighteenth century, and the deeper root of pendere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：expenditure 的首见年代只能大致定在十八世纪，pendere 的更早词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same weighing-out verb that are often swapped by mistake; group two holds words for money laid out, each with a different scope.
note.cn: 第一组同出「称出、付出」这一动词，常被误用互换；第二组都指付出去的钱，但范围不同。

entries.definition: The older noun for one cost or for the burden of a cost; expenditure is the collective total, often institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的名词，指一笔费用或费用带来的负担；expenditure 指汇总的总额，多用于机构。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to lay out money, energy or effort; it cannot stand where the noun is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指付出金钱、精力或努力；不能占据名词的位置。

entries.definition: An adjective describing something that costs a lot, not a record of money already spent.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述某物花费高，而不是已花掉的钱的记录。

entries.definition: The common noun for money spent, close in meaning but plainer in tone and less tied to budgets.
entries.definitionCN: 指花掉的钱的常用名词，意思接近，但语气更普通，与预算的联系较弱。

entries.definition: What must be paid for something, whether or not it has been paid yet; expenditure records what has been laid out.
entries.definitionCN: 为某物必须支付的代价，无论是否已支付；expenditure 记录的是已经付出的部分。

entries.definition: Money paid at the start of a project or purchase, often a single large sum.
entries.definitionCN: 项目或采购开始时付出的一笔钱，常指一次较大的支出。

entries.definition: A plan for future spending; it is the intention, while expenditure is what actually leaves the account.
entries.definitionCN: 对未来支出的计划，是意图；expenditure 是真正离开账户的钱。

entries.definition: The regular sums a household or small business must pay, such as rent and bills.
entries.definitionCN: 家庭或小企业必须定期支付的开销，如房租与账单。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations take the real image of weighing money, the real family and the real budget phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想取「称量钱币」这一真实意象、真实词族与真实预算搭配。

normal.en: The root means 'to weigh': spending was once silver weighed out on a scale.
normal.cn: 词根意为「称量」：花钱曾经就是把银子放在秤上称出。

normal.en: The family runs expend, expense, expenditure, expensive, expendable.
normal.cn: 词族包括 expend、expense、expenditure、expensive、expendable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the budget sense: public expenditure, capital expenditure, household expenditure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出预算义：公共开支、资本支出、家庭支出。

normal.en: Expenditure is the total; expense is the single bill.
normal.cn: expenditure 是总额，expense 是单笔账单。

normal.en: The word usually answers the question 'how much was spent in the year', not 'what did this item cost'.
normal.cn: 这个词通常回答「这一年花了多少」，而不是「这件东西多少钱」。

abstract.en: Picture a scale on a merchant's table where coins are weighed before they leave the purse.
abstract.cn: 想象商人桌上的一杆秤，硬币在离开钱袋之前先被称过。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger in which every column is a different kind of need.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账册，每一栏都是一种不同的需要。

abstract.en: Picture a reservoir being drained in measured bucketfuls rather than all at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一座水库被一桶一桶地计量放水，而不是一次抽干。

examples.en: The city increased expenditure on public transport by a modest amount.
examples.cn: 该市小幅增加了公共交通支出。

examples.en: Capital expenditure on the bridge was spread over three years.
examples.cn: 这座桥的资本支出分摊在三年内。

examples.en: Household expenditure responds quickly to changes in fuel prices.
examples.cn: 家庭支出对燃料价格的变化反应很快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一开支（expend）就心疼（花掉的那部分）」——钱一笔笔花出去，汇总起来就是支出

root: 拉丁语 expendere（称出、付出）＝ex-（向外）＋pendere（悬挂、称量）；其名词 expensa 指付出的钱。英语 expenditure 由 expend 加表行为或结果的后缀构成，十八世纪出现。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: value is weighed and handed out, and the same movement is then scaled up to a period total, cut into single entries, split by sector, and finally applied to energy and patience.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把价值称量后交出去；这个动作再被放大为期间总额、切成单笔记录、按部门划分，最后用到能量与耐心上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: coins weighed on a scale before they leave the purse.
core.cn: 核心意象：硬币在离开钱袋前先放在秤上称量。

branches.en: TOTAL AND ACT: one side of the ledger is named both as a sum and as the act of paying it out.
branches.cn: 总额与行为：账目的一侧既被当作一个总和，也被当作付出这笔钱的动作。

branches.en: SINGLE ENTRY: keeping accounts line by line cuts the mass into countable pieces.
branches.cn: 单笔记录：逐行记账把整块支出切成可数的片段。

branches.en: SECTOR SPLIT: households and long-lived assets each get their own column, one for daily living and one for future capacity.
branches.cn: 部门切分：家庭与长期资产各得一栏，一栏用于日常生计，一栏用于未来产能。

branches.en: PUBLIC BUDGET: the state's outlay becomes a political total that is argued over in the open.
branches.cn: 公共预算：国家的支出成为公开争论的政治总额。

branches.en: OTHER RESERVES: energy and patience can be paid out too, so the word outgrows money.
branches.cn: 其他储备：能量与耐心同样可以被付出，于是这个词超出了金钱的范围。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb plus an English noun suffix, and both halves recur in ordinary accounting vocabulary.
intro.cn: 这个词是一个拉丁动词加一个英语名词后缀，两部分都在日常会计词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere gives expend, expense and expenditure; the prefix marks the direction outward.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 衍生出 expend、expense 与 expenditure；前缀标出「向外」的方向。

items.example: The prefix points the movement of money away from the payer.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀指出钱从付款人那里向外流出。

items.structure: pendere, pependi, pensum (Latin verb, third conjugation)
items.example: The root joins hanging, weighing and paying in one image.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把悬挂、称量与支付合成一个意象。

items.example: Expendere names the act behind the English noun.
items.exampleCN: expendere 点明英语名词背后的动作。

items.meaning: to lay out money or effort
items.example: They expended most of the grant on equipment.
items.exampleCN: 他们把大部分拨款用在设备上。

items.example: Travel expenses were paid in arrears.
items.exampleCN: 差旅费事后报销。

items.example: Expenditure rose with the new term.
items.exampleCN: 新学年开始后支出上升。

items.example: The repair proved expensive.
items.exampleCN: 这次修理花费很高。

items.example: The older units were treated as expendable.
items.exampleCN: 较旧的装置被视为可舍弃的。

definition_en: the money needed for something, or the cost or sacrifice that something involves
core_image: 餐桌上摊着一叠小票，每一张都对应一次不得不付的钱
scene: 月底对着一叠小票逐张核对，加起来的数目比预想的更沉。The repairs were a considerable expense, but the roof no longer leaked.
sceneCN: 一张张收据被摊开核对，总额超出预想；句中的 expense 指「为某事必须付出的费用」（第 1 个义项：办成某事所需的那笔钱）。图中可辨识物件：收据、计算器、笔、信封、账单。

senses.title: Money needed for a purpose
senses.definition: the money that has to be paid in order to do or obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 为做成或获得某物而必须支付的钱
senses.example: The repairs were a considerable expense, but the roof no longer leaked.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理花了不少钱，但屋顶不再漏水了。
senses.why: The noun comes straight from the idea of money weighed out, and its first job is to name the sum a purpose demands.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词直接来自「把钱称出去」的观念，它最初的职责就是指出某个目的所需的款项。

senses.title: A cost item in accounts
senses.definition: a particular cost recorded in a business's books, such as rent, travel or materials
senses.definitionCN: 记在企业账簿上的一笔特定成本，如房租、差旅或材料
senses.example: The company claimed the training as a business expense.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把这笔培训费作为营业费用申报。
senses.why: Business accounting needs each outflow to sit in its own line, so a mass noun becomes a countable item.
senses.whyCN: 商业会计需要让每一笔流出各占一行，于是不可数名词变成了可数的项目。

senses.title: The act of spending
senses.definition: the act of paying money out, especially on a regular or official basis
senses.definitionCN: 付出钱款的行为，尤指经常性或公务性的付出
senses.example: The office keeps a strict record of expense each quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 该办公室每季度严格记录花销。
senses.why: Like many nouns of Latin origin, it can name either the act or its object, and older usage often prefers the act.
senses.whyCN: 像许多源自拉丁语的名词一样，它既可指动作也可指对象，较早的用法常偏指动作。

senses.title: A reimbursed staff account
senses.definition: an arrangement by which an employer pays back money an employee has spent on its behalf
senses.definitionCN: 雇主向员工偿还在公务中垫付的钱的一种安排
senses.example: She put the client dinner on her expense account.
senses.exampleCN: 她把请客户吃饭的费用记在报销账户上。
senses.why: A fixed phrase turns the abstract noun into a concrete piece of office machinery.
senses.whyCN: 一个固定搭配把抽象名词变成了一件具体的办公工具。

senses.title: A cost borne by someone else
senses.definition: the loss or disadvantage that one person or group suffers so that another may gain
senses.definitionCN: 一方为让另一方获益而承受的损失或不利
senses.example: The factory cut costs at the expense of local water quality.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂以当地水质为代价削减成本。
senses.why: From 'money paid' the word slides to 'price paid' in a wider sense, and the payer can be someone other than the buyer.
senses.whyCN: 从「付出的钱」滑向更广的「付出的代价」，而承担代价的人未必是购买者。

senses.title: Cost in time or effort
senses.definition: the time, effort or risk that an activity costs, measured without money
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动所耗的时间、精力或风险，并不以金钱计量
senses.example: The move was worthwhile but involved great expense of time.
senses.exampleCN: 这次搬迁值得做，但耗费了大量时间。
senses.why: Once expense means 'what must be given up', any limited resource can be its currency.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 expense 意为「必须交出去的东西」，任何有限的资源都可以充当它的货币。

senses.title: Unlimited spending on an occasion
senses.definition: the willingness to pay any amount for a particular occasion or result
senses.definitionCN: 为某个场合或结果愿意支付任何数额的钱
senses.example: They spared no expense on the opening ceremony.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在开幕式上不惜工本。
senses.why: The negative construction treats expense as a limit, and denying the limit produces the sense of lavishness.
senses.whyCN: 否定式把 expense 当作一个限度，否认这个限度就产生了「铺张」的意思。

senses.title: A person or thing that drains money
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：不断耗钱的人或物
senses.definition: a person, habit or possession that regularly takes money to keep
senses.definitionCN: 需要不断花钱来维持的人、习惯或所有物
senses.example: The old car had become an expense rather than a convenience.
senses.exampleCN: 那辆旧车已从便利变成了负担。
senses.why: The word can name not the sum but the source of the sums, which is why speakers call a costly thing an expense.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不去指金额，而指金额的来源，所以人们会把耗钱的东西本身称作 expense。

intro.en: Expense came through Old French from Latin expensa, the feminine past participle of expendere 'to weigh out, pay out', used as a noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: expense 经古法语来自拉丁语 expensa，即 expendere「称出、付出」的阴性过去分词作名词用。年代为约数。

items.en: Pendere meant 'to hang' and 'to weigh'; because payments were weighed, it also meant 'to pay'. Its deeper root is a reconstruction.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂」与「称量」；由于付款要称重，它也指「支付」。其更早词根属重构形式。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pendere gave expendere, 'to weigh out and pay out'.
items.cn: 表「向外」的前缀加 pendere 构成 expendere，意为「称出并付出」。

items.en: The participle expensa came to be used as a noun meaning 'money paid out', the form English borrowed.
items.cn: 分词 expensa 被用作名词，意为「付出的钱」，英语借入的正是这个形式。

items.en: Old French espense carried the word into English in the thirteenth century, first as a record of money spent.
items.cn: 古法语 espense 在十三世纪把这个词带入英语，最初指已花钱的记录。

items.en: By the sixteenth century expense could mean any cost or sacrifice, including the loss one party bears for another's gain.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，expense 已可指任何代价或牺牲，包括一方为另一方获益而承受的损失。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date at which the 'sacrifice' sense appeared is not established, and the pre-Latin root of pendere is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：表示「牺牲」的义项出现的确切年代未得到证明，pendere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the same money-outflow family, where the difference is scope rather than meaning; group two holds other words for a cost.
note.cn: 第一组同属「钱向外流」的词族，差别在范围而非词义；第二组是其他表示代价的词。

entries.definition: The total spent over a period, usually by an institution; expense is a single cost or the burden it creates.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内的支出总额，通常指机构的；expense 指单笔费用或由此产生的负担。

entries.definition: To lay out money, energy or effort; it is the action behind both nouns.
entries.definitionCN: 付出金钱、精力或努力；它是两个名词背后的动作。

entries.definition: Describes something that costs a lot; it is a judgement about price, not a recorded cost.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物花费高；它是对价格的判断，而不是记录下来的费用。

entries.definition: The plural usually names sums spent on behalf of an employer and later repaid.
entries.definitionCN: 复数通常指为雇主垫付、事后报销的款项。

entries.definition: The amount that must be paid or suffered for something; broader than expense because it covers harm as well as money.
entries.definitionCN: 为某物必须支付或承受的量；比 expense 更宽，因为它也涵盖损害。

entries.definition: The price asked by a seller or service provider on a bill.
entries.definitionCN: 卖方或服务方在账单上索要的价格。

entries.definition: Money paid at the start of a project, often a large single amount.
entries.definitionCN: 项目开始时付出的一笔钱，常指一次较大的支出。

entries.definition: The amount requested for a good; it becomes an expense only when it is actually paid by the buyer.
entries.definitionCN: 为商品索要的金额；只有买方真正付出时，它才变成费用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real weighing image, the real family and the real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的称量意象、真实词族与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: The word once meant silver weighed out, so every expense is a small weighing.
normal.cn: 这个词曾指称出的银子，因此每一笔费用都是一次小小的称量。

normal.en: The family runs expend, expense, expenditure, expensive, expensively.
normal.cn: 词族包括 expend、expense、expenditure、expensive、expensively。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the social side: at the expense of, expense account, spare no expense.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显出它的社会面向：以为代价、报销账户、不惜工本。

normal.en: The plural expenses usually means money advanced for an employer.
normal.cn: 复数 expenses 通常指为雇主垫付的钱。

normal.en: Expense is the single bill; expenditure is the total.
normal.cn: expense 是单笔账单；expenditure 是总额。

abstract.en: Picture a receipt folded into a wallet that is already too thin.
abstract.cn: 想象一张收据被折进一个本就很薄的钱包。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that never balances: one pan holds goods, the other holds what they cost.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆永远不平的秤：一边放货物，另一边放它们所耗的钱。

abstract.en: Picture a house that looks free to live in but sends a bill every month.
abstract.cn: 想象一座看似免费居住的房子，却每月寄来账单。

examples.en: The expense of moving abroad was greater than they had planned for.
examples.cn: 移居国外的费用比他们原先计划的高。

examples.en: Every expense over the limit needs a receipt and a signature.
examples.cn: 超过限额的每一笔费用都需要收据与签字。

examples.en: He built his career at the expense of his health.
examples.cn: 他以健康为代价建立了自己的事业。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一支出（ex）就破费（pense）」——钱称出去，换来一件东西或一次经历

root: 拉丁语 expensa（付出的钱），来自 expendere（称出、付出）＝ex-（向外）＋pendere（悬挂、称量）；经古法语 espense 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bill: money leaves the payer, and the same word then names an account line, the act of paying, a sacrifice borne by someone else, a cost in time, unlimited spending, and finally the thing that keeps generating bills.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一张账单展开：钱从付款人手里离开；同一个词再依次指账目中的一行、付款的动作、由他人承受的牺牲、时间上的代价、不计限度的花费，最后指不断产生账单的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a receipt for money that had to be handed over.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张为不得不交出的钱开出的收据。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND ACT: the necessary sum and the act of paying it are one event seen as a thing and as a deed.
branches.cn: 金额与行为：必需的款项与付出它的动作，是同一件事被看成物与被看成事。

branches.en: BOOKKEEPING: each cost gets a line, and a line meant for staff spending gets a fixed name.
branches.cn: 记账：每笔成本各得一行，专供员工垫付的那一行另有固定名称。

branches.en: WIDER PRICE: what is paid can be another person's water or one's own time, so money stops being the only currency.
branches.cn: 更宽的代价：被付出的可以是别人的水质或自己的时间，金钱不再是唯一货币。

branches.en: NO LIMIT: denying the limit turns expense into a display of wealth.
branches.cn: 没有限度：否认限度，就把费用变成了财力的展示。

branches.en: SOURCE OF BILLS: a costly possession is itself called an expense because it keeps producing them.
branches.cn: 账单的来源：耗钱的物品本身被称为费用，因为它不断制造账单。

intro.en: The word is a Latin participle turned noun, and its prefix and root also build the verb and the adjective beside it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁分词转成的名词，其前缀与词根还构成它旁边的动词与形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin pendere and expendere supply expense; the same root reaches English through several French-shaped forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pendere 与 expendere 提供 expense；同一词根经几个法语形式进入英语。

items.example: The prefix marks money moving out of the purse.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出钱从钱袋向外移动。

items.example: Weighing was the original act of paying.

items.example: Expensa was the bookkeeper's word.
items.exampleCN: 这是记账人用的词。

items.example: The expense was shared between the partners.
items.exampleCN: 费用由合伙人分摊。

definition_zh: 支出结构；支出模式（各类开销在总支出中的比例与走向）
definition_en: the way spending is distributed across categories, and how that distribution changes over time
core_image: 一张分成几栏的账页，食品、房租、交通各占一条高低不同的色带，色带整体缓慢移动
scene: 账本摊开，几类开销被画成高低不同的色带，食品、房租与交通各自占去一块。The survey found that the expenditure pattern of city households had shifted towards services.
sceneCN: 账页上几类开销被画成高低不同的色带，各占一块；句中的 expenditure pattern 指「各类支出在总支出中的分布方式」（第 1 个义项：按类别划分的支出构成）。图中可辨识物件：分类账页、彩色条带、比例尺、铅笔、计算器。

collocations.phrase: a change in the expenditure pattern

derivatives.zh: 有图案的；按模式形成的

senses.title: How spending is split across categories
senses.titleCN: 支出在各类别之间的分配方式
senses.definition: the shares of total spending that go to different categories such as food, housing and transport
senses.definitionCN: 总支出中分给食品、住房、交通等不同类别的份额
senses.example: The survey found that the expenditure pattern of city households had shifted towards services.
senses.exampleCN: 调查发现，城市家庭的支出结构已向服务倾斜。
senses.why: A pattern is a shape repeated across parts, so the phrase names the shape that spending makes when it is divided by category.
senses.whyCN: 模式是各部分重复呈现的形状，因此这个短语指支出按类别切分后所呈现的形状。

senses.title: A household's habitual way of spending
senses.definition: the recurring way a household distributes its income among needs and wants
senses.definitionCN: 家庭在需要与想要之间反复分配收入的惯常方式
senses.example: Their expenditure pattern leaves little room for savings.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的支出模式几乎没有留下储蓄空间。
senses.why: Repetition is the core of pattern: a single month is a set of bills, but twelve similar months make a pattern.
senses.whyCN: 重复是模式的要点：单月只是一叠账单，十二个相似的月份才构成模式。

senses.title: A statistical trend over time
senses.titleCN: 随时间变化的统计走势
senses.definition: a measurable direction of change in the composition of spending across successive periods
senses.definitionCN: 连续时期内支出构成的可测量的变化方向
senses.example: Official figures show a steady expenditure pattern over the decade.
senses.exampleCN: 官方数据显示，这十年间的支出走势相当平稳。
senses.why: Statistics turns the household habit into a line on a chart, and the line itself is called a pattern.
senses.whyCN: 统计把家庭习惯变成图表上的一条线，而这条线本身也被称作模式。

senses.title: A regional or national structure
senses.titleCN: 地区或国家的支出结构
senses.definition: the typical distribution of spending across a region, income group or whole economy
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区、收入群体或整个经济的典型支出分布
senses.example: The expenditure pattern of the coastal provinces differs from that of inland ones.
senses.exampleCN: 沿海省份的支出结构与内陆省份不同。
senses.why: Once aggregated, individual habits become a social fact, and the phrase is used for whole populations.
senses.whyCN: 一旦加总，个人习惯就成了社会事实，这个短语便用于整个群体。

senses.title: A company's spending profile
senses.definition: the split of a firm's outgoings among wages, materials, marketing and other headings
senses.definitionCN: 企业支出在工资、材料、营销等科目之间的划分
senses.example: Auditors compared the firm's expenditure pattern with its rivals.
senses.exampleCN: 审计人员将该公司的支出结构与竞争对手作了比较。
senses.why: Firms also keep category accounts, so the same phrase transfers from households to balance sheets.
senses.whyCN: 企业同样按类别记账，因此同一个短语从家庭账本转到了资产负债表。

senses.title: A shift in the composition
senses.definition: a recognised change in the relative weight of categories, as when services take a larger share
senses.definitionCN: 各类别相对权重的显著变化，例如服务所占份额变大
senses.example: Rising incomes produced a marked shift in the expenditure pattern.
senses.exampleCN: 收入上升使支出结构出现明显转变。
senses.why: The word pattern invites comparison, and comparison makes change visible, so the phrase often appears with shift or change.
senses.whyCN: 「模式」一词天然引出比较，比较又让变化显现，因此这个短语常与「转变」「变化」连用。

senses.title: An analytical template in economics
senses.definition: a standard classification used by economists to compare spending across households or countries
senses.definitionCN: 经济学家用来比较家庭或国家支出的标准分类框架
senses.example: The model takes the expenditure pattern as its starting input.
senses.exampleCN: 该模型以支出结构作为起始输入。
senses.why: Here pattern is no longer observed behaviour but a fixed shape imposed for comparison.
senses.whyCN: 这里的模式不再是观察到的行为，而是为了比较而设定的固定框架。

senses.title: Any repeatable allocation of resources
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何可重复的资源分配方式
senses.definition: any stable way of dividing limited resources among competing claims, whether money, time or attention
senses.definitionCN: 在相互竞争的需求之间分配有限资源的任何稳定方式，无论资源是金钱、时间还是注意力
senses.example: The laboratory's expenditure pattern favours equipment over staff.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验室的资源分配方式偏向设备而非人员。
senses.why: Generalised beyond money, the phrase describes any recurring budget of scarce means.
senses.whyCN: 超出金钱范围后，这个短语描述任何稀缺手段的重复分配方案。

intro.en: The phrase joins expenditure, an English noun from Latin expendere 'to weigh out, pay', with pattern, which reached English from Latin patronus 'protector' through Old French. The compound itself belongs to modern statistical economics. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由 expenditure 与 pattern 组成：前者是英语名词，来自拉丁语 expendere「称出、付出」；后者经古法语来自拉丁语 patronus「保护人」。复合短语本身属于近代统计经济学。年代为约数。

items.en: Ex- 'out' plus pendere 'to weigh' produced expendere, 'to weigh out and pay out'; its noun expensa gave English expense and, later, expenditure.
items.cn: 表「向外」的前缀加 pendere「称量」构成 expendere「称出、付出」，其名词 expensa 给英语带来 expense，后来又有了 expenditure。

items.en: Patronus meant 'protector, patron', derived from pater 'father'. It named the person who stood in a protective role.
items.cn: patronus 意为「保护人、庇护者」，由 pater「父亲」派生，指居于保护地位的人。

items.en: Old French patron passed into English in the fourteenth century; the same form split into patron, for a supporter, and pattern, for a model to be copied.
items.cn: 古法语 patron 在十四世纪进入英语；同一形式后来分化为 patron（支持者）与 pattern（可供模仿的范本）。

items.en: By the sixteenth century pattern had moved from 'an example to copy' to 'a repeated arrangement of parts', which is the sense economics later used.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，pattern 已从「供人模仿的范例」转为「各部分重复出现的排列」，经济学后来用的正是这个义项。

items.en: The full phrase appears in twentieth-century household-budget studies and national accounts, where spending is classified and compared.
items.cn: 完整短语出现在二十世纪的家庭预算研究与国民经济核算中，那里对支出进行分类与比较。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first use of the exact phrase is not recorded precisely, and the shift of pattern from 'model' to 'recurring form' is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个确切短语的首见记录无法精确定位；pattern 从「范本」转为「重复形态」的年代亦只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds the two halves of the phrase and their near variants, which are often confused; group two holds other ways of describing how money is divided.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两半及其近似变体，常被混用；第二组是其他描述钱如何分配的说法。

entries.definition: The total money spent; it says nothing about how the total is divided.
entries.definitionCN: 指花掉的总金额，并不说明总额如何划分。

entries.definition: A single charge or the burden of it, too small a unit to form a distribution.
entries.definitionCN: 指单笔费用或费用负担，单位太小，构不成一种分布。

entries.definition: The everyday synonym; it is equally correct but less formal than the phrase with expenditure.
entries.definitionCN: 日常同义说法，同样正确，但不如含 expenditure 的说法正式。

entries.definition: On its own it can mean a printed design; only with expenditure does it name a budget structure.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时可以指印花图案；只有与 expenditure 连用才指预算结构。

entries.definition: The formal economic term for the same division of household spending, common in translated statistical reports.
entries.definitionCN: 同一家庭支出划分的正式经济术语，常见于统计报告译本。

entries.definition: The intended division of a budget; it is a plan, while an expenditure pattern is observed.
entries.definitionCN: 预算的预期划分，是计划；而支出结构是观察到的实况。

entries.definition: A person's usual way of spending, stressing behaviour rather than measurable shares.
entries.definitionCN: 个人惯常的花钱方式，强调行为而非可计量的份额。

entries.definition: The act of assigning resources to purposes; it names the decision, not the resulting shape.
entries.definitionCN: 把资源分配给用途的动作，指决定本身，而非由此形成的形状。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real halves of the phrase, the real family and the real statistical context.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用短语真实的两半、真实词族与真实统计语境。

normal.en: Expenditure is the total; pattern is the shape it makes when divided.
normal.cn: expenditure 是总额，pattern 是它被划分后形成的形状。

normal.en: The family runs expend, expense, expenditure, pattern, patterned.
normal.cn: 词族包括 expend、expense、expenditure、pattern、patterned。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the analysis: household expenditure pattern, a shift in the pattern.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分析语境：家庭支出结构、结构的转变。

normal.en: The phrase answers 'what share goes where', not 'how much in total'.
normal.cn: 这个短语回答「各占多少份额」，而不是「总共多少」。

normal.en: Economics compares patterns; budgets plan totals.
normal.cn: 经济学比较结构，预算则规划总额。

abstract.en: Picture a pie cut into slices whose widths slowly change from year to year.
abstract.cn: 想象一块馅饼被切成若干片，各片的宽窄逐年缓慢变化。

abstract.en: Picture a graph whose bars swap heights without the total moving much.
abstract.cn: 想象一张图，各条柱子的高低互换，而总量几乎不变。

abstract.en: Picture a household that quietly spends less on food and more on fares each decade.
abstract.cn: 想象一个家庭，每过十年就悄悄少花些饭钱、多花些车费。

examples.en: Rising rents changed the expenditure pattern of young workers.
examples.cn: 租金上涨改变了年轻劳动者的支出结构。

examples.en: The report compares the expenditure pattern of rural and urban households.
examples.cn: 该报告比较了农村与城市家庭的支出结构。

examples.en: A stable expenditure pattern makes next year's budget easier to draft.
examples.cn: 稳定的支出结构让来年预算更容易起草。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「支出（expenditure）排成花样（pattern）」——各类开销按比例摆出的花样，就是支出结构

root: 拉丁语 expendere（称出、付出）＋拉丁语 patronus（保护人，经古法语 patron 转为「范本、花样」）；前者给出 expenditure，后者给出 pattern。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a total is divided into categories, and the same division is read as a household habit, a trend, a regional fact, a corporate profile, a visible shift, a comparison template and finally any recurring budget of scarce means.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形状展开：总额被切成类别，这个切分再被读成家庭习惯、时间走势、地区事实、企业概况、可见的转变、比较用的框架，最后泛指任何稀缺手段的重复分配。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a page of accounts divided into bands of different widths.
core.cn: 核心意象：一页账目被分成宽窄不同的色带。

branches.en: SHAPE AND HABIT: one month shows shares, twelve months show a routine.
branches.cn: 形状与习惯：一个月显出份额，十二个月显出惯例。

branches.en: SCALE: the same shape is read as a trend in time and as a structure across a region.
branches.cn: 尺度：同一形状在时间上读作走势，在地域上读作结构。

branches.en: FIRM: a company's headings reproduce the household's categories on a balance sheet.
branches.cn: 企业：公司的科目在资产负债表上复现了家庭的类别。

branches.en: CHANGE: comparing two shapes makes a shift visible, which is why the phrase travels with words for change.
branches.cn: 变化：比较两个形状就让转变显形，因此这个短语常与表示变化的词同行。

branches.en: TEMPLATE: once fixed for comparison, the shape can be imposed on any scarce resource.
branches.cn: 框架：一旦为比较而固定，这个形状就可以套到任何稀缺资源上。

intro.en: The phrase has two transparent halves: one for money laid out, one for a repeated shape, and both are built from Latin nouns and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个短语的两半都很透明：一半指付出的钱，一半指重复的形状，两者都由拉丁名词与动词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin expendere supplies the first half; Latin patronus, through Old French, supplies the second.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 expendere 提供前半，拉丁语 patronus 经古法语提供后半。

items.example: The prefix marks the outward flow of money.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出金钱向外流出。

items.example: Payment began as weighing.
items.exampleCN: 支付最初就是称量。

items.example: The verb underlies expenditure.
items.exampleCN: 动词构成 expenditure 的基础。

items.example: Expenditure rose with the price of fuel.
items.exampleCN: 支出随燃料价格上升。

items.example: The root names the protecting father.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根点明保护者的父亲角色。

items.example: Patronus named the one who shielded others.
items.exampleCN: patronus 指庇护他人的人。

items.example: The word moved from model to repeated form.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从「范本」转为「重复形态」。

items.example: The cloth was patterned with small squares.
items.exampleCN: 布上印着小方格图案。

items.example: The expenditure pattern shifted towards services.
items.exampleCN: 支出结构向服务倾斜。

definition_zh: 收入；赚得的钱；工资；（公司）盈利
definition_en: money earned by working or by an asset, or the profit that a company reports to its owners
core_image: 周五傍晚，一叠工钱被装进信封，信封边角因反复摩挲而发软
scene: 周五傍晚，工钱装进信封，信封边角被反复摩挲得发软。Her earnings barely covered the rent, so she took a second shift.
sceneCN: 工钱在周五傍晚装进信封，薄得几乎盖不住房租；句中的 earnings 指「靠劳动赚来的钱」（第 1 个义项：工资性的劳动所得）。图中可辨识物件：工资信封、工资条、打卡钟、饭盒、硬币。

pos.zh: 收入；工资；盈利（常用复数形式）

derivatives.zh: 挣钱的人；能带来收益的事物

senses.title: Money earned by working
senses.definition: the money a person receives in return for work, especially wages or salary
senses.definitionCN: 个人因工作而得到的钱，尤指工资或薪金
senses.example: Her earnings barely covered the rent, so she took a second shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她的收入几乎不够付房租，于是又接了一个班。
senses.why: The noun is simply the plural of what has been earned, so its first sense is the sum that work brings in.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词就是「所挣得之物」的复数，因此第一个义项是劳动带来的那笔钱。

senses.title: Company profit reported to owners
senses.titleCN: 公司向股东报告的盈利
senses.definition: the profit a company makes in a period, as reported to shareholders
senses.definitionCN: 公司在一段时期内赚得、并向股东报告的利润
senses.example: The firm reported earnings above forecasts.
senses.exampleCN: 该公司报告的盈利高于预期。
senses.why: For a company, what it earns is what remains after costs, so the same word moves from wages to profit.
senses.whyCN: 对公司而言，所「挣得」的就是扣除成本后的剩余，于是同一个词从工资转到利润。

senses.title: Profit measured per share
senses.definition: a company's profit divided by the number of shares, used as a standard measure of performance
senses.definitionCN: 公司利润除以股数得出的数值，用作衡量业绩的标准指标
senses.example: Earnings per share fell after the new shares were issued.
senses.exampleCN: 增发新股之后，每股收益下降。
senses.why: Investors need a common yardstick across firms of different size, so earnings are divided by shares.
senses.whyCN: 投资者需要一把能横量不同规模公司的尺子，于是把盈利除以股数。

senses.title: The scheduled profit announcement
senses.definition: the quarterly or annual statement in which a company makes its profit public
senses.definitionCN: 公司公开其利润的季度或年度报表
senses.example: Investors waited for the earnings report before buying.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者等到盈利报告发布后才买入。
senses.why: A recurring event needs a short name, and the thing announced supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 反复发生的事件需要一个简短名称，被公布的内容便充当了这个名称。

senses.title: Profit after deductions
senses.titleCN: 扣除各项之后的净收益
senses.definition: profit remaining after tax, interest and other charges have been subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 扣除税款、利息及其他费用后剩下的利润
senses.example: Net earnings rose despite flat sales.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管销售持平，净收益仍然上升。
senses.why: Accounting reports several layers of profit, and the last layer keeps the plain name with a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 会计分几层报告利润，最后一层保留原名而另加限定词。

senses.title: Profit kept inside the business
senses.titleCN: 留在企业内部的留存收益
senses.definition: profit that is not paid out to owners but kept in the business for future use
senses.definitionCN: 不分配给所有者、而留在企业内备用的利润
senses.example: The board moved part of retained earnings into reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会把一部分留存收益转入准备金。
senses.why: Once profit can be either distributed or kept, the kept portion needs its own fixed phrase.
senses.whyCN: 一旦利润可以被分配或被保留，被保留的那部分就需要自己的固定说法。

senses.title: Return from savings or assets
senses.titleCN: 储蓄或资产带来的收益
senses.definition: the income produced by money saved, lent or invested rather than by work
senses.definitionCN: 由储蓄、借贷或投资的钱而非劳动产生的收入
senses.example: Bond earnings are taxed as ordinary income.
senses.exampleCN: 债券收益按普通收入征税。
senses.why: Anything that yields a return can be said to earn, so the plural covers interest and dividends as well as wages.
senses.whyCN: 任何能带来回报的东西都可以说在「挣」，因此这个复数也涵盖利息与股息，而不只是工资。

senses.title: What effort or risk brings in
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：努力或风险换来的回报
senses.definition: the return that any effort, patience or risk eventually produces
senses.definitionCN: 任何努力、耐心或风险最终带来的回报
senses.example: Years of quiet work produced modest earnings.
senses.exampleCN: 多年默默工作只带来有限的回报。
senses.why: At its widest the word measures what comes back from what was put in, whether the input was labor or capital.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽的意义上，这个词衡量投入之后回流的东西，无论投入的是劳动还是资本。

intro.en: Earnings is the plural noun from the Old English verb earnian 'to earn, deserve, work for', which belongs to the Germanic stock and has no Latin cognate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: earnings 是由古英语动词 earnian「挣得、应得、为……劳作」而来的复数名词；该词属日耳曼语源，没有拉丁同族词。年代为约数。

items.en: The verb goes back to a Germanic stem meaning 'to labour, earn', represented in Old Frisian and Old High German as well as Old English.
items.cn: 这个动词可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「劳作、挣得」的词干，在古弗里斯语与古高地德语中也有对应形式。

items.en: Earnian meant 'to deserve, to earn, to work for', so the oldest sense joins labour with what labour merits.
items.cn: earnian 意为「应得、挣得、为……劳作」，因此最古老的意义把劳动与劳动所应得之物连在一起。

items.en: In Middle English the verb widened from deserving to gaining money by work, and the idea of wages became central.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，这个动词从「应得」扩展到「靠劳动获得金钱」，工资的意味成为核心。

items.en: The plural noun earnings, meaning 'that which is earned', is recorded in the eighteenth century and later became a standard term in wages and accounting.
items.cn: 复数名词 earnings 意为「所挣得之物」，在十八世纪有记录，后来成为工资与会计中的标准用语。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word was attached to corporate profit, to profit per share and to the scheduled report of both.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词被用于公司利润、每股利润以及两者的定期报告。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of the Germanic stem is unknown, and the exact first date of the plural noun is not established; there is no Latin cognate, so the Latin list is empty.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个日耳曼词干的更早来源不明，复数名词的确切首见年代亦未得到证明；没有拉丁同族词，因此拉丁词条留空。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same earning verb that differ only in grammar; group two holds words for money received, each covering a different source.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个「挣得」动词的不同形式，差别只在语法；第二组都指收到的钱，但来源不同。

entries.definition: To gain money by work or to deserve something; it cannot occupy the place of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 靠劳动获得金钱或应得某物；不能占据名词的位置。

entries.definition: The person who earns, as in a wage earner; earnings is the money, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 挣钱的人，如工薪者；earnings 指钱，不指人。

entries.definition: Describes income gained by work, as opposed to unearned income from property.
entries.definitionCN: 描述靠劳动获得的收入，与来自财产的非劳动收入相对。

entries.definition: Describes income that comes without work, such as rent or inherited wealth.
entries.definitionCN: 描述无需劳动而得的收入，如租金或继承的财富。

entries.definition: All money received in a period, from work, investments or transfers; it is the widest of these words.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间内收到的全部钱款，来自工作、投资或转移支付；是这些词中范围最宽的。

entries.definition: Pay calculated by time or output, usually for manual or hourly work.
entries.definitionCN: 按时间或产量计算的报酬，通常指体力或计时工作。

entries.definition: A fixed sum paid regularly, usually monthly or yearly, for professional work.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定周期支付的报酬，通常按月或按年，针对专业工作。

entries.definition: The total money a company receives from sales before costs are deducted; earnings is what remains after costs.
entries.definitionCN: 公司在扣成本前从销售中收到的总金额；earnings 是扣除成本后剩下的部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Germanic history, the real word family and the real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的日耳曼语演变、真实词族与真实会计搭配。

normal.en: The oldest sense joined work with what work deserves: earn meant both 'labour for' and 'deserve'.
normal.cn: 最古老的意义把劳动与劳动所应得之物连在一起：这个词既指「为……劳作」，也指「应得」。

normal.en: The family runs earn, earner, earnings, earned, unearned.
normal.cn: 词族包括 earn、earner、earnings、earned、unearned。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the financial sense: earnings per share, earnings report, retained earnings.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金融义：每股收益、盈利报告、留存收益。

normal.en: Earnings is plural in form but takes a plural verb only when separate sums are meant.
normal.cn: earnings 形式上是复数，但只有指多笔不同款项时才接复数动词。

normal.en: Keep the contrast: revenue is money coming in, earnings is money left after costs.
normal.cn: 记住对比：revenue 是进来的钱，earnings 是扣除成本后留下的钱。

abstract.en: Picture a pay envelope thin enough that the rent notice looks thicker.
abstract.cn: 想象一只薄薄的工资信封，薄到房租通知看起来更厚。

abstract.en: Picture a column of numbers in a report that shareholders read before their coffee cools.
abstract.cn: 想象报表里的一列数字，股东在咖啡凉透前就读完了。

abstract.en: Picture a seed that returns a handful of grain only after a whole season of work.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子，要经过整季劳作才换回一把谷粒。

examples.en: Average earnings in the region have lagged behind prices.
examples.cn: 该地区的平均收入落后于物价。

examples.en: The company's earnings were hit by higher energy costs.
examples.cn: 该公司的盈利受到能源成本上升的打击。

examples.en: Savings account earnings are modest but stable.
examples.cn: 储蓄账户的收益不高，但很稳定。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「饿（ear）着肚子也要挣（earn）」——靠劳动换来的钱，就是收入

root: 古英语 earnian（挣得、应得、为……劳作），属日耳曼语源，更早词干来源不确定；无拉丁同族词。英语 earnings 为「所挣得之物」的复数名词，十八世纪起通行。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one envelope: money comes back from work, and the same word then measures a company's profit, that profit per share, the report announcing it, the layers left after deductions, the part kept inside, the return from assets, and finally the yield of any effort.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一只信封展开：劳动换回钱；同一个词再用来衡量公司利润、每股利润、公布利润的报告、扣除后的各层剩余、留在企业内的部分、资产带来的回报，最后指任何努力的产出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pay envelope that is thinner than the bills it must cover.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只工资信封，薄到盖不住它要应付的账单。

branches.en: LABOUR: the oldest sense ties earning to work and to what work fairly deserves.
branches.cn: 劳动：最古老的意义把「挣得」与劳动、以及劳动应得之物绑在一起。

branches.en: CORPORATE PROFIT: a firm's earnings are its profit, and the report that announces them borrows the same word.
branches.cn: 公司利润：企业的「所挣」就是利润，公布它的报告也借用同一个词。

branches.en: PER SHARE: profit is divided by shares so that firms of different size can be compared.
branches.cn: 按股计量：利润除以股数，使规模不同的公司可以相互比较。

branches.en: LAYERS: deductions leave net earnings, and the part not distributed becomes retained earnings.
branches.cn: 层次：各项扣除后剩下净收益，未分配的部分成为留存收益。

branches.en: ANY RETURN: interest, dividends and the yield of effort all repeat the shape of something coming back.
branches.cn: 任何回报：利息、股息与努力的产出，都重复「有东西回流」这一形状。

intro.en: Earnings is a native Germanic word with an English plural suffix; its ending marks a mass of results rather than a single coin.
intro.cn: earnings 是英语本族的日耳曼语词，加上英语复数后缀；词尾标记的是一堆结果，而不是一枚硬币。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin ancestor; the Germanic verb earnian is its source, so no Latin entries are listed.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖先，其来源是日耳曼语动词 earnian，因此不列拉丁词条。

items.example: She earns a modest wage.
items.exampleCN: 她挣一份不高的工资。

items.example: The ending turns the verb into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种活动。

items.meaning: more than one; a mass of
items.example: The plural gathers many payments into one sum.
items.exampleCN: 复数把多笔款项聚成一个总和。

items.example: Earnings rose with the new contract.
items.exampleCN: 新合同签订后收入上升。

items.example: Both earners in the household work full time.
items.exampleCN: 这家的两个挣钱人都做全职。

items.example: Earned income is taxed differently.
items.exampleCN: 劳动所得按不同方式征税。

items.example: Rent is often called unearned income.
items.exampleCN: 租金常被称为非劳动收入。

items.example: The earnings report surprised the market.
items.exampleCN: 盈利公告令市场意外。

derivatives.zh: 挣钱的人；能带来收益的事物

definition_en: the money gained after costs are paid, or any advantage gained from an action
core_image: 集市收摊后，两张桌子并排：一张放本钱，一张放收回的钱，后者多出一小堆
scene: 集市收摊后，摊主把本钱与收回的钱分放两处，收回的那边多出一小堆。After a strong season, the bakery finally turned a profit.
sceneCN: 摊主把本钱和货款分开放，货款那边多出一小堆；句中的 profit 指「扣除成本后剩下的钱」（第 1 个义项：经营所得减去成本后的净增益）。图中可辨识物件：两张木桌、钱箱、账本、面包篮、收摊的布。

senses.title: Money left after costs
senses.definition: the money that remains from income after all costs of producing or selling have been paid
senses.definitionCN: 收入在支付全部生产或销售成本后剩下的钱
senses.example: After a strong season, the bakery finally turned a profit.
senses.exampleCN: 经过一个旺季，这家面包店终于开始盈利。
senses.why: The Latin root means 'to make progress', and profit is the advance a business makes beyond what it spent.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「向前推进」，而利润就是企业在收回花费之后向前多走的那一步。

senses.title: Gain from a single sale
senses.definition: the gain made when something is sold for more than it cost
senses.definitionCN: 把某物以高于成本的价格卖出时得到的增益
senses.example: They sold the old press at a profit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把旧印刷机卖掉，赚了一笔。
senses.why: A single transaction repeats the whole logic in miniature: buy low, sell higher, keep the difference.
senses.whyCN: 单笔交易把整套逻辑缩小重演：低价买入、高价卖出、留下差额。

senses.title: The motive to seek gain
senses.definition: the incentive to act because of the gain expected, especially in economic life
senses.definitionCN: 因预期收益而行动的驱动力，尤见于经济生活
senses.example: The profit motive drove the expansion into new markets.
senses.exampleCN: 营利动机推动企业向新市场扩张。
senses.why: Once profit is a regular result, it becomes a reason for acting, and the word names the reason.
senses.whyCN: 一旦利润成为常规结果，它就成了行动的理由，而这个词也就用来指这个理由。

senses.title: Gross profit before deductions
senses.definition: sales revenue minus the direct cost of goods, before other expenses are subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 销售收入减去商品的直接成本，尚未扣除其他费用
senses.example: Gross profit looked healthy, but rent ate most of it.
senses.exampleCN: 毛利看起来不错，但房租吃掉了大半。
senses.why: Accounts separate direct costs from overheads, so profit is split into layers and the first layer gets a qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 会计把直接成本与间接费用分开，于是利润被分层，第一层配上一个限定词。

senses.title: Net profit after all charges
senses.titleCN: 扣除全部费用后的净利润
senses.definition: the final profit after every cost, tax and charge has been subtracted
senses.definitionCN: 扣除所有成本、税款与费用之后的最终利润
senses.example: Net profit for the year was smaller than the headline figure suggested.
senses.exampleCN: 全年净利润比标题数字所显示的要少。
senses.why: The last layer is what owners actually keep, so it is marked off from the earlier, flattering layers.
senses.whyCN: 最后一层才是所有者真正留下的，因此要与前面那些更好看的层次区分开。

senses.title: Profit as a ratio of sales
senses.titleCN: 以销售额为基准的利润率
senses.definition: profit expressed as a percentage of revenue, showing how much of each sale is kept
senses.definitionCN: 以收入百分比表示的利润，显示每笔销售能留下多少
senses.example: A thin profit margin leaves little room for a price cut.
senses.exampleCN: 利润率很薄，几乎没有降价空间。
senses.why: Absolute profit cannot compare firms of different size, so it is turned into a margin, a share of each sale.
senses.whyCN: 绝对利润无法比较规模不同的企业，于是把它转成利润率，即每笔销售中的占比。

senses.title: Advantage in a broad sense
senses.definition: a benefit or advantage gained from an activity, not necessarily financial
senses.definitionCN: 从某项活动中获得的益处，未必与金钱有关
senses.example: He read the old manuals to his profit.
senses.exampleCN: 他读那些旧手册，从中获益。
senses.why: Before profit was narrowed to money, it meant any forward gain, and that older sense survives in formal writing.
senses.whyCN: 在利润被收窄为金钱之前，它泛指任何前进式的获益，这一旧义仍存于正式书面语中。

senses.title: Any gain from an action
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何行动带来的净增益
senses.definition: whatever is gained from an action once its costs, including effort and risk, are counted
senses.definitionCN: 把努力与风险等代价计入后，行动所带来的任何净增益
senses.example: The expedition showed a profit in knowledge if not in money.
senses.exampleCN: 这次考察若不以金钱计，则在知识上有收益。
senses.why: Generalised, profit is simply the surplus of return over outlay, whatever the currency of each side.
senses.whyCN: 一般化之后，利润就是回报超出投入的剩余，无论两边用的是什么「货币」。

intro.en: Profit came through Old French from Latin profectus 'progress, advance', the past participle of proficere 'to accomplish', built on pro- 'forward' and facere 'to do, make'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: profit 经古法语来自拉丁语 profectus「进展、前进」，它是 proficere「完成、取得进展」的过去分词，由表「向前」的前缀与 facere「做、造」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Facere meant 'to do, make'. Its deeper root is reconstructed, and it is the source of a very large family including effect, factory and difficult.
items.cn: facere 意为「做、造」。其更早词根属重构形式，它是包括 effect、factory、difficult 在内一大族词的来源。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus facere produced proficere, 'to make progress, to accomplish, to be useful'.
items.cn: 表「向前」的前缀加 facere 构成 proficere，意为「取得进展、完成、有用」。

items.en: Its past participle profectus was used as a noun for 'progress, advance, gain', the sense that passed into French.
items.cn: 其过去分词 profectus 被用作名词，指「进展、前进、增益」，这一意义传入了法语。

items.en: Old French prufit or profit meant 'advantage, gain', and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century first as a general benefit.
items.cn: 古法语 prufit 或 profit 意为「好处、增益」，英语在十四世纪借入，最初泛指益处。

items.en: The financial surplus sense hardened in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, and gross, net and margin later divided it into layers.
items.cn: 财务盈余义在十六、十七世纪逐渐固定；后来毛利、净利与利润率又把它分成几层。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date of the financial sense is not settled, and the pre-Latin root of facere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：财务义的确切出现年代没有定论，facere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes and sound-alikes, including one that is not related at all; group two holds words for money gained, each measured at a different point.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词，其中有一个根本不同源；第二组都指获得的钱，但计量的位置不同。

entries.definition: A person who foretells the future, from Greek prophētēs 'one who speaks for a god'; it sounds identical to profit but shares no root.
entries.definitionCN: 指预言未来的人，来自希腊语 prophētēs「代神发言者」；与 profit 同音，却完全不同源。

entries.definition: Describes something that yields profit; it cannot replace the noun that names the gain itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述能带来利润的事物；不能取代指利润本身的名词。

entries.definition: Someone who makes excessive profit, especially in a shortage; the ending adds a tone of blame.
entries.definitionCN: 指牟取过厚利润的人，尤见于短缺时期；词尾带有谴责语气。

entries.definition: Yielding no gain; it negates the adjective rather than naming a loss.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有收益的；它否定的是形容词，而不是指亏损。

entries.definition: An increase in money or advantage; broader and less technical than profit.
entries.definitionCN: 金钱或好处的增加；比 profit 更宽泛，也不那么技术化。

entries.definition: The profit a company reports to its owners, often used interchangeably with profit in finance.
entries.definitionCN: 公司向所有者报告的利润，在金融语境中常与 profit 互用。

entries.definition: Money received from sales before any cost is deducted; profit is what survives the deduction.
entries.definitionCN: 销售中收到的钱，尚未扣除任何成本；profit 是扣除后幸存的部分。

entries.definition: The gain on an investment expressed as a proportion of what was put in.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收益按投入比例表示的增益。

entries.definition: The amount by which income exceeds outgoings, often used of public accounts rather than private firms.
entries.definitionCN: 收入超出支出的部分，常用于公共账目而非私人企业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin steps, the real family and the real accounting phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁语演变、真实词族与真实会计搭配。

normal.en: The root means 'to make forward': profit is the step a business takes beyond its costs.
normal.cn: 词根意为「向前做成」：利润就是企业越过成本向前多走的一步。

normal.en: The family runs profit, profitable, profitability, profitably, profiteer.
normal.cn: 词族包括 profit、profitable、profitability、profitably、profiteer。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the accounts: gross profit, net profit, profit margin.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出账目层次：毛利、净利、利润率。

normal.en: The same root appears in factory and effect, both built on the verb 'to make'.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 factory 与 effect 中，二者都建立在「做」这个动词上。

normal.en: Profit is what is left; revenue is what came in.
normal.cn: 利润是留下来的；收入是进来的。

abstract.en: Picture two piles on a table, one for what was spent and one for what came back.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上两堆钱，一堆是花出去的，一堆是收回来的。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder whose lowest rung is cost and whose top rung is what the owner keeps.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子，最下面一级是成本，最上面一级是所有者留下的。

abstract.en: Picture a market stall that packs up only after the till is heavier than the stock was.
abstract.cn: 想象一个摊位，只有钱箱比原先的货更沉时才收摊。

examples.en: The cooperative distributes its profit among the members.
examples.cn: 合作社把利润分配给成员。

examples.en: Rising costs squeezed the profit margin to almost nothing.
examples.cn: 成本上升把利润率压到几乎为零。

examples.en: She studied the old maps to her profit.
examples.cn: 她研读旧地图，从中获益。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「不（pro）费（fit）」——成本没有白费，多出来的那部分就是利润

root: 拉丁语 profectus（进展、增益），来自 proficere（取得进展）＝pro-（向前）＋facere（做、造）；经古法语 profit 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one surplus: something comes back larger than it went out, and the word then names a single sale's gain, the motive behind it, the layered accounts of gross and net, the margin, an older sense of general benefit, and finally any surplus of return over outlay.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一份剩余展开：回流之物比付出之物更大；这个词再指单笔交易的赚头、背后的动机、毛利与净利的分层账目、利润率、较早的泛指益处，最后指任何回报超出投入的剩余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two piles of money on a table, and the returning pile is the taller one.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上两堆钱，收回来那堆更高。

branches.en: SURPLUS: the whole business and a single sale both end with more than they began with.
branches.cn: 剩余：整个生意与单笔交易都以「比开始时多」收尾。

branches.en: MOTIVE: expected gain becomes the reason to act, and the word shifts from result to cause.
branches.cn: 动机：预期收益成为行动的理由，这个词便从结果转指原因。

branches.en: LAYERS: direct costs and overheads cut the surplus into gross and net.
branches.cn: 分层：直接成本与间接费用把剩余切成毛利与净利。

branches.en: RATIO: dividing profit by sales makes it comparable across firms.
branches.cn: 比率：把利润除以销售额，使它能在企业之间比较。

branches.en: OLD AND GENERAL: the earliest sense of any forward benefit survives in formal prose and then widens to every kind of return.
branches.cn: 旧义与泛义：最早的「任何前进式益处」存于正式书面语，继而扩展到各种回报。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb 'to make', and the family around it keeps that same shape.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀加一个意为「做」的拉丁动词构成，周围的词族也保持同样的结构。

latinIntro.en: Latin pro- and facere build proficere and its participle profectus, which French shortened into the noun English took over.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的前缀与 facere 构成 proficere 及其分词 profectus，法语将其缩短为英语接手的名词。

items.example: The prefix gives the sense of moving ahead.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀赋予「向前走」的意思。

items.example: The root is one of the busiest in English.

items.example: The verb names moving forward by doing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指靠「做」向前推进。

items.example: The participle became a noun of advance.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词变成了表示前进的名词。

items.example: The year ended with a small profit.
items.exampleCN: 这一年以小额利润收尾。
