definition_zh: 有利可图的；能盈利的；有益的
definition_en: producing a financial gain, or bringing a useful advantage of some other kind
core_image: 果园主人翻着账本，发现改种之后每一季的收成都能盖过成本并有余
scene: 果园主人翻着账本，发现改种之后每一季的收成都能盖过成本。The orchard became profitable once the new varieties replaced the old ones.
sceneCN: 果园主人对着账本核算，改种后每季收成超过成本；句中的 profitable 指「能带来经济盈余的」（第 1 个义项：收入超过成本的）。图中可辨识物件：账本、果篮、修枝剪、地契、计算器。

pos.zh: 有利可图的；能盈利的；有益的

senses.title: Producing a financial gain
senses.definition: producing more money than it costs to run or make
senses.definitionCN: 带来的钱多于运转或制造它所花的钱
senses.example: The orchard became profitable once the new varieties replaced the old ones.
senses.exampleCN: 新品种取代旧品种后，这片果园开始盈利。
senses.why: The adjective simply says that a thing possesses the quality of yielding profit, so its core sense is financial.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是说某物具有「带来利润」的性质，因此它的核心义是财务上的。

senses.title: Able to be run at a gain
senses.definition: described of a business or venture that can be operated without losing money
senses.definitionCN: 形容一种能够不亏本地经营下去的业务或项目
senses.example: Small farms are rarely profitable without subsidies.
senses.exampleCN: 没有补贴，小农场很少能盈利。
senses.why: Applied to an undertaking, the word is about viability over time rather than one good month.
senses.whyCN: 用于一项事业时，这个词讲的是长期能否维持，而不是某一个月走运。

senses.title: Worth doing for the advantage
senses.definition: worth doing because it brings an advantage, even when no money is involved
senses.definitionCN: 因为能带来好处而值得做，即使不涉及金钱
senses.example: It is profitable to compare the two accounts before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 在决定之前比较这两份说法是有益的。
senses.why: The old sense of profit as any advantage lets the adjective leave the marketplace.
senses.whyCN: profit 早先泛指任何益处，这使这个形容词得以离开市场语境。

senses.title: Yielding a useful result
senses.definition: described of a discussion, lesson or method that produces a useful result
senses.definitionCN: 形容讨论、课程或方法产生了有用的结果
senses.example: The two teams held a profitable exchange of data.
senses.exampleCN: 两个团队进行了一次有益的数据交流。
senses.why: If an activity yields something worth having, the same adjective can call it gainful in a non-financial way.
senses.whyCN: 如果一项活动产出了值得拥有的东西，同一个形容词就可以在不涉及金钱的意义上说它有收益。

senses.title: Returning more than it costs
senses.definition: described of an investment whose return exceeds the sum put in
senses.definitionCN: 形容回报超过投入金额的投资
senses.example: The solar installation proved profitable within six years.
senses.exampleCN: 这套太阳能设备在六年内就收回了成本并开始获利。
senses.why: Investment is profit imagined in advance, so the adjective marks the point where the return crosses the cost.
senses.whyCN: 投资就是预先设想的利润，因此这个形容词标出回报越过成本的那一点。

senses.title: Worth cultivating or working
senses.definition: described of land, a crop or a trade that pays for the work it demands
senses.definitionCN: 形容土地、作物或行业能抵偿其所耗的劳动
senses.example: Olives are more profitable than wheat on these dry slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些干燥的坡地上，橄榄比小麦更有利可图。
senses.why: Agriculture applies the word to the land itself, asking whether the harvest pays for the labour.
senses.whyCN: 农业把这个词直接用在土地上，问的是收成是否抵得上劳动。

senses.title: Showing a profit in the accounts
senses.definition: described of a period whose accounts show a surplus rather than a loss
senses.definitionCN: 形容某段时期的账目显示盈余而非亏损
senses.example: It was the first profitable quarter since the factory reopened.
senses.exampleCN: 那是工厂重开以来第一个盈利的季度。
senses.why: Once accounts are kept by period, an adjective is needed to label the periods that end in surplus.
senses.whyCN: 账目一旦按时期记录，就需要一个形容词来标记那些以盈余收尾的时期。

senses.title: Any activity whose returns exceed costs
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：收益超过代价的任何活动
senses.definition: described of any activity whose returns, in money, knowledge or well-being, exceed what it consumes
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何活动，其在金钱、知识或福祉上的回报超过它所消耗的
senses.example: A habit of reading is profitable over a lifetime, though not in a ledger.
senses.exampleCN: 阅读的习惯在一生中都是有益的，尽管账本上看不出来。
senses.why: At its widest the adjective compares every kind of return with every kind of cost.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽的意义上，这个形容词比较各种回报与各种代价。

intro.en: Profitable joins profit, from Latin profectus 'advance', with the Latin-derived suffix -able meaning 'capable of'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: profitable 由 profit 加源自拉丁语、意为「能够……」的后缀构成；profit 来自拉丁语 profectus「前进、增益」。年代为约数。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus facere 'to make' gave proficere, 'to accomplish or make progress'.
items.cn: 表「向前」的前缀加 facere「做、造」构成 proficere，意为「完成、取得进展」。

items.en: The participle profectus supplied the noun for 'advance, gain', which Old French shortened to profit.
items.cn: 分词 profectus 提供了表示「前进、增益」的名词，古法语将其缩短为 profit。

items.en: English had the noun by the fourteenth century, first in the broad sense of benefit or advantage.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪已有这个名词，最初泛指好处或益处。

items.en: The suffix came from Latin -abilis, 'able to be', and had already produced many English adjectives before it was attached to profit.
items.cn: 这个后缀来自拉丁语 -abilis「能够被……」，在接到 profit 之前已构成许多英语形容词。

items.en: Profitable is recorded in the late fourteenth century, and its financial sense hardened as accounting vocabulary grew.
items.cn: profitable 在十四世纪晚期已有记录，随着会计词汇的发展，其财务义逐渐固定。

items.en: Source uncertain: the precise first citation of the adjective is not settled, and the pre-Latin root of facere is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个形容词的确切最早书证没有定论，facere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective's own family, where grammar rather than meaning makes the difference; group two holds adjectives that also promise a good return.
note.cn: 第一组是这个形容词自身的词族，差别在语法而非词义；第二组是同样承诺「有好回报」的形容词。

entries.definition: The gain itself; the adjective describes something that yields it.
entries.definitionCN: 指增益本身；形容词则描述能带来增益的事物。

entries.definition: The noun for the degree of gain, used when the quality is measured rather than simply asserted.
entries.definitionCN: 指获利程度的名词，用于该性质被计量而非仅仅断言时。

entries.definition: Modifies an action, telling how it was carried out; it cannot describe a business directly.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰动作，说明以何种方式完成；不能直接描述一家企业。

entries.definition: Losing money or yielding no advantage; the direct opposite, not a milder word.
entries.definitionCN: 亏钱或没有益处；是直接的反义，而非语气更轻的说法。

entries.definition: Producing a large amount of money; stronger than profitable, which only says costs are covered.
entries.definitionCN: 产生大量金钱；比 profitable 语气更强，后者只说盖过成本。

entries.definition: Giving satisfaction or a sense of worth, usually without any financial claim.
entries.definitionCN: 带来满足感或价值感，通常不含财务上的意思。

entries.definition: Worth the time or effort spent; it need not involve money at all.
entries.definitionCN: 值得花费时间或精力；完全不涉及金钱也可以。

entries.definition: Able to keep going as a business; viability is about survival, profitability about surplus.
entries.definitionCN: 作为企业能够维持下去；可行性讲生存，盈利能力讲盈余。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix, the real family and the real phrases of trade and accounts.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀、真实词族与真实的交易与账目搭配。

normal.en: Profit plus the suffix 'able to be': able to yield a gain.
normal.cn: profit 加表示「能够」的后缀：能够带来收益的。

normal.en: The family runs profit, profitable, profitability, profitably, unprofitable.
normal.cn: 词族包括 profit、profitable、profitability、profitably、unprofitable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the business sense: profitable business, profitable investment, profitable year.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：有利可图的生意、有利可图的投资、盈利的年份。

normal.en: The word answers 'does it pay', not 'how much does it pay'.
normal.cn: 这个词回答「划不划算」，而不是「能赚多少」。

normal.en: Profitable is the judgement; profitability is the measurement.
normal.cn: profitable 是判断，profitability 是计量。

abstract.en: Picture an orchard where the fruit sold covers the cost of every ladder and basket.
abstract.cn: 想象一片果园，卖果子的钱抵得上每一架梯子和每一只篮子。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that leaves both people with something they can use.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话，让两个人都带着能用的东西离开。

abstract.en: Picture a machine that returns more power than it takes to run.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器，输出的动力多于维持它运转所需的。

examples.en: The shop made the switch to local suppliers because it proved profitable.
examples.cn: 这家店改用地本供应商，因为事实证明这样做有利可图。

examples.en: Not every profitable habit shows up in a bank account.
examples.cn: 并非每个有益的习惯都会体现在银行账户里。

examples.en: The most profitable line was the one with the fewest returns.
examples.cn: 最赚钱的产品线是退货最少的那一条。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「profit（利润）＋表示『能够』的后缀」——能把成本盖过、还能剩下钱的，就是有利可图的

root: profit（拉丁语 profectus「增益」，来自 proficere「取得进展」＝pro-「向前」＋facere「做」）＋一个源自拉丁语、表示「能够被……」的后缀（拉丁语 -abilis）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one test: does what comes back exceed what goes in? The test is applied first to a business, then to an undertaking, a decision, a discussion, an investment, a crop, an accounting period and finally to any activity at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一道检验展开：回来的是否多于出去的？这道检验依次用于企业、事业、决定、讨论、投资、作物、会计期间，最后用于任何活动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a harvest that weighs more than the labour it took.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份收成，其重量超过为它付出的劳动。

branches.en: ENTERPRISE: the first test is whether a business or venture pays for itself over time.
branches.cn: 企业：第一道检验是生意或项目能否长期抵偿自身成本。

branches.en: DECISION AND TALK: money drops out, and the test becomes whether an action or discussion leaves something useful.
branches.cn: 决定与谈话：金钱退场，检验变成行动或讨论是否留下有用的东西。

branches.en: INVESTMENT: the moment the return crosses the sum put in.
branches.cn: 投资：回报越过投入金额的那一刻。

branches.en: LAND: a crop or slope is judged by whether the harvest repays the labour.
branches.cn: 土地：作物或坡地以其收成是否偿还劳动来评判。

branches.en: PERIOD AND LIFE: an accounting period can show surplus, and a whole life can be called gainful without a ledger.
branches.cn: 期间与一生：会计期间可以显示盈余，而一生即使没有账本也可说是有收益的。

intro.en: The adjective is a noun plus a suffix of capacity, and the noun itself is a Latin participle turned into a French-shaped word.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由一个名词加一个表示「能力」的后缀构成，而那个名词本身是拉丁分词变成的法语式词。

latinIntro.en: Latin profectus gives profit; Latin -abilis gives the ending that turns it into an adjective of possibility.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 profectus 提供 profit；拉丁语 -abilis 提供词尾，把它变成表示可能性的形容词。

items.example: The prefix adds direction to the making.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给「做」加上了方向。

items.example: The root is visible in factory and effect.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在 factory 与 effect 中可见。

items.example: The participle became the noun of gain.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词成了表示增益的名词。

items.example: Profit is the base of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 利润是这个形容词的基础。

items.example: The suffix turns a noun into a capacity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把名词变成一种能力。

items.example: The venture became profitable.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目变得有利可图。

items.example: The land is used profitably.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地被有收益地利用。

items.example: Profitability is measured by ratios.
items.exampleCN: 盈利能力用比率来衡量。

items.example: The route was unprofitable and closed.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线无利可图，已停运。

definition_zh: 盈利能力；获利性；利润水平
definition_en: the ability of a business or activity to produce a profit, or the measured degree of that ability
core_image: 几张报表并排摊开，每张都用一条斜线标出「每一元钱能带回多少」
scene: 董事会把几张报表并排摊开，逐行比较每一条业务线能带回多少。Analysts questioned the profitability of the new plant.
sceneCN: 董事们并排比对报表，逐条业务线核算回报；句中的 profitability 指「一项业务产生利润的能力」（第 1 个义项：企业或业务持续获利的能力）。图中可辨识物件：并排的报表、折线、比例尺、钢笔、咖啡杯。

pos.zh: 盈利能力；获利性；利润水平

forms.label: 复数（罕用，指多种获利水平）

senses.title: The ability to produce profit
senses.definition: the capacity of a business, product or activity to produce a profit rather than a loss
senses.definitionCN: 企业、产品或活动产生利润而非亏损的能力
senses.example: Analysts questioned the profitability of the new plant.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师质疑新工厂的盈利能力。
senses.why: The suffix turns the adjective into a quality, so the noun names the capacity that a profitable thing has.
senses.whyCN: 后缀把形容词变成一种性质，因此这个名词指「有利可图之物」所具备的能力。

senses.title: The measured degree of gain
senses.definition: the extent to which an operation earns more than it costs, expressed as a figure or a level
senses.definitionCN: 一项经营赚得超过成本的程度，以数字或水平表示
senses.example: Profitability fell from one quarter to the next.
senses.exampleCN: 盈利能力从一个季度到下一个季度下降。
senses.why: A quality that can rise and fall must be measurable, and the noun is used for the measurement itself.
senses.whyCN: 一种能升能降的性质必然可计量，这个名词就用于指那个计量结果。

senses.title: A financial ratio or indicator
senses.definition: one of the standard ratios, such as return on sales or on capital, used to express gain
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示获利的标准比率之一，如销售回报率或资本回报率
senses.example: The report lists three measures of profitability.
senses.exampleCN: 报告列出三项盈利能力指标。
senses.why: Accounting prefers ratios because they compare firms of different size, so the abstract noun becomes a family of indicators.
senses.whyCN: 会计偏好比率，因为比率能比较规模不同的企业，于是这个抽象名词变成一组指标。

senses.title: A management goal
senses.definition: a target that managers pursue when they try to raise the surplus earned on each sale
senses.definitionCN: 管理者为提高每笔销售所赚盈余而追求的目标
senses.example: Improving profitability became the board's first priority.
senses.exampleCN: 提高盈利能力成为董事会的首要任务。
senses.why: Once measured, a quality can be aimed at, and the noun moves from description to objective.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可计量，一种性质就能成为瞄准的对象，这个名词便从描述转为目标。

senses.title: The level across a sector
senses.definition: the average ability of firms in an industry or region to earn a surplus
senses.definitionCN: 某一行业或地区的企业平均赚取盈余的能力
senses.example: Sector-wide profitability has fallen since the price cap.
senses.exampleCN: 自价格上限实施以来，整个行业的盈利能力下降。
senses.why: Comparisons are usually made between groups, so the noun is applied to aggregates rather than single firms.
senses.whyCN: 比较通常在群体之间进行，因此这个名词被用于加总体，而不是单个企业。

senses.title: Sustained gain over the long run
senses.definition: the ability to keep earning a surplus across many years and through downturns
senses.definitionCN: 在多年间、穿越衰退仍持续赚取盈余的能力
senses.example: Long-term profitability matters more to pension funds than a single strong year.
senses.exampleCN: 对养老基金而言，长期盈利能力比单独一个丰收年更重要。
senses.why: Investors with long horizons care about durability, so the noun acquires a time dimension.
senses.whyCN: 长期投资者看重持久性，这个名词因此带上时间维度。

senses.title: The gain of a specific product line
senses.titleCN: 某一产品线的获利情况
senses.definition: the surplus earned by one product, service or branch compared with the rest
senses.definitionCN: 某一产品、服务或分支相较于其余部分所赚的盈余
senses.example: They discontinued the line despite its early profitability.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管这条产品线早期获利，他们还是把它停掉了。
senses.why: Firms need to know which part pays for the others, so the noun is attached to individual units.
senses.whyCN: 企业需要知道哪一部分在养活其余部分，因此这个名词被挂到具体单元上。

senses.title: The quality of yielding more than cost
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：收益高于代价的性质
senses.definition: the general quality of any arrangement that returns more than it consumes
senses.definitionCN: 任何安排所具有的「回报多于消耗」的一般性质
senses.example: The charity judged the profitability of the scheme in hours saved, not money.
senses.exampleCN: 该慈善机构以节省的工时而非金钱来衡量这项方案的收益。
senses.why: Stripped of ledgers, the noun still compares return with cost, whatever units are used on either side.
senses.whyCN: 剥去账本之后，这个名词仍在比较回报与代价，无论两边用的是什么单位。

intro.en: Profitability is profitable plus the Latin-derived suffix -ity, which turns an adjective into a noun of quality. The word belongs to modern commercial and statistical writing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: profitability 由 profitable 加源自拉丁语、把形容词转为性质名词的后缀构成。这个词属于近代商业与统计写作。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun profit goes back to profectus 'advance, gain', from proficere 'to make progress'.
items.cn: 名词 profit 可追溯到 profectus「前进、增益」，来自 proficere「取得进展」。

items.en: Profitable, formed with the suffix of capacity, is recorded in the late fourteenth century.
items.cn: profitable 由表示「能力」的后缀构成，在十四世纪晚期已有记录。

items.en: The suffix -ity continues Latin -itas, which names a state or quality and reached English through French forms.
items.cn: 表示性质的后缀承自拉丁语 -itas，用来指状态或性质，并经法语形式进入英语。

items.en: Profitability appears in nineteenth-century commercial writing, when firms began to compare returns by ratio rather than by absolute sum.
items.cn: profitability 出现在十九世纪的商业写作中，当时企业开始用比率而非绝对金额比较回报。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became a standard heading in financial analysis, management targets and sector studies.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成为财务分析、管理目标与行业研究中的标准条目。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of profitability is not established, and the pre-Latin root of the verb behind profit is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：profitability 的确切最早书证未得到证明，profit 背后那个动词在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the adjective, the noun of gain and the measured noun, which are constantly swapped; group two holds other measures of financial health.
note.cn: 第一组是形容词、表示增益的名词与表示计量结果的名词，常被互换误用；第二组是其他衡量财务健康的概念。

entries.definition: Says that something yields a gain; the noun names the capacity or its measured level.
entries.definitionCN: 说某物能带来收益；名词则指这种能力或其计量水平。

entries.definition: The gain itself in money; profitability is the ability or degree, not the sum.
entries.definitionCN: 指金钱上的增益本身；profitability 是能力或程度，不是金额。

entries.definition: Describes how an action is performed; it cannot serve as the subject of a sentence about performance.
entries.definitionCN: 描述动作如何执行；不能充当讨论业绩的句子主语。

entries.definition: The practice of taking excessive gain, especially in a shortage; it carries blame that profitability does not.
entries.definitionCN: 指在短缺等情况下牟取过厚利润的做法；带谴责意味，而 profitability 没有。

entries.definition: The gain on an investment as a proportion of what was put in; it can refer to a single asset rather than a whole business.
entries.definitionCN: 投资收益占投入的比例；可指单项资产，而非整个企业。

entries.definition: The part of each sale that is kept as profit; a narrower measure than profitability.
entries.definitionCN: 每笔销售中留作利润的部分；比盈利能力更窄的指标。

entries.definition: The ratio of output to input; a firm can be efficient and still unprofitable if prices are too low.
entries.definitionCN: 产出与投入之比；企业可以很高效，却因价格过低而无利可图。

entries.definition: The ability to meet debts as they fall due; it concerns survival, not surplus.
entries.definitionCN: 到期偿还债务的能力；关乎生存，而非盈余。

entries.definition: The ability of an organisation or plan to survive; profitability adds the requirement of a surplus.
entries.definitionCN: 组织或计划维持下去的能力；盈利能力则额外要求有盈余。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real suffix chain, the real accounting phrases and the real distinction from the sum itself.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的后缀链条、真实会计搭配，以及它与金额本身的真实区别。

normal.en: Profitable plus the suffix of quality gives the name of the quality: the ability to earn a surplus.
normal.cn: profitable 加表示性质的后缀，就得到这种性质的名字：赚取盈余的能力。

normal.en: The family runs profit, profitable, profitability, profitably, unprofitable.
normal.cn: 词族包括 profit、profitable、profitability、profitably、unprofitable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the analysis: profitability ratio, profitability analysis, long-term profitability.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出分析语境：盈利能力比率、盈利能力分析、长期盈利能力。

normal.en: Profit is a number; profitability is a rate or a capacity.
normal.cn: 利润是一个数字；盈利能力是一种比率或能力。

normal.en: A firm can post a profit and still have weak profitability if its capital is huge.
normal.cn: 一家企业可以录得利润，若资本庞大，盈利能力仍然偏弱。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across a report to show how much each unit of money brings back.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子横放在报表上，量出每一单位钱能带回多少。

abstract.en: Picture a plant that keeps producing fruit year after year without being replanted.
abstract.cn: 想象一株植物年年结果，而无需重新栽种。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that compares what a workshop consumes with what it sends out.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，比较一间作坊消耗的东西与它送出的东西。

examples.en: The merger was intended to lift profitability rather than to cut jobs.
examples.cn: 这次合并意在提高盈利能力，而非裁减岗位。

examples.en: Farm profitability depends heavily on the price of fuel.
examples.cn: 农业的盈利能力在很大程度上取决于燃料价格。

examples.en: They measured profitability per hectare rather than per worker.
examples.cn: 他们按每公顷而非每名工人衡量盈利能力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「profit（利润）＋表示『能力』的后缀」——能持续赚出利润的本事，就是盈利能力

root: profitable（profit 来自拉丁语 profectus「增益」，加表「能够」的后缀）＋一个源自拉丁语、表示性质或状态的后缀（拉丁语 -itas）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one question: how well does this pay? The question is asked of a capacity, a measured level, a ratio, a target, a sector, a long horizon, a single product line and finally of any arrangement that returns more than it consumes.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个问题展开：这件事有多划算？问题依次指向一种能力、一个计量水平、一项比率、一个目标、一个行业、一段长期、一条产品线，最后指向任何回报高于消耗的安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler laid across accounts to measure what each unit of money brings back.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子横在账目上，量出每一单位钱能带回多少。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND LEVEL: the quality exists first as an ability, then as a figure that rises or falls.
branches.cn: 能力与水平：这种性质先作为能力存在，再作为一个会升会降的数字存在。

branches.en: RATIO: to compare firms of different size, the ability is expressed as a proportion.
branches.cn: 比率：为比较规模不同的企业，这种能力被表示成比例。

branches.en: TARGET: a measured quality can be aimed at, so description becomes an objective.
branches.cn: 目标：可计量的性质能成为瞄准的对象，描述于是变成目标。

branches.en: UNIT OF ANALYSIS: the same measure is applied to a whole sector and to a single product line.
branches.cn: 分析单元：同一项度量既用于整个行业，也用于单条产品线。

branches.en: TIME AND GENERALITY: durability adds a long horizon, and the idea finally leaves money behind.
branches.cn: 时间与泛化：持久性加上长期维度，这个观念最终离开金钱语境。

intro.en: The noun stacks three pieces: a Latin participle turned noun, a suffix of capacity, and a suffix of quality.
intro.cn: 这个名词叠了三层：拉丁分词转成的名词、表示能力的后缀，以及表示性质的后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin profectus supplies profit, Latin -abilis supplies the adjective ending, and Latin -itas supplies the final noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 profectus 提供 profit，拉丁语 -abilis 提供形容词词尾，拉丁语 -itas 提供最终的名词词尾。
