items.exampleCN: 这个前缀给出增益的方向。

items.example: The root underlies profit.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根构成 profit 的基础。

items.example: Profit is the first layer.
items.exampleCN: 利润是第一层。

items.example: The suffix yields profitable.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀构成 profitable。

items.example: The line is profitable.
items.exampleCN: 这条产品线是有利可图的。

items.example: The suffix turns the adjective into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把形容词变成一种性质。

items.example: Profitability improved after the reform.
items.exampleCN: 改革后盈利能力提高。

items.example: The fleet operates profitably.
items.exampleCN: 这支船队以获利的方式运营。

items.example: The branch was unprofitable for years.
items.exampleCN: 这个分支多年无利可图。

definition_zh: 丧失；损失；亏损；死亡；减少
definition_en: the fact of no longer having something, the money lost in business, or a decrease in amount
core_image: 一只抽屉被拉开，原本放手表的位置空着，只剩一圈浅浅的印痕
scene: 抽屉被拉开，原本放手表的格子空着，只留下一圈浅浅的印痕。The loss of the old workshop hit the village harder than anyone expected.
sceneCN: 抽屉里原本放手表的位置空着，只剩印痕；句中的 loss 指「不再拥有某物这一事实」（第 1 个义项：失去占有或拥有）。图中可辨识物件：拉开的抽屉、空表位、圆形印痕、旧钥匙、灰尘。

senses.title: No longer having something
senses.definition: the fact or experience of no longer having something that one had
senses.definitionCN: 不再拥有曾经拥有之物的这一事实或经历
senses.example: The loss of the old workshop hit the village harder than anyone expected.
senses.exampleCN: 老作坊的失去对村庄的打击比任何人预想的都重。
senses.why: The word names the state left behind when a possession or condition is no longer there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指某物或某种状态不在之后留下的那个空缺状态。

senses.title: A person or thing that is missed
senses.titleCN: 被怀念、被惋惜的人或物
senses.definition: a person or thing whose absence is felt as a deprivation by a group
senses.definitionCN: 其缺席被群体感受为缺失的人或物
senses.example: The retired teacher was a great loss to the school.
senses.exampleCN: 这位退休教师对学校是一大损失。
senses.why: Instead of the event of losing, the word can name the thing whose absence is felt.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以不指「失去」这件事，而指那个缺席被感受到的人或物。

senses.title: Money lost in business
senses.definition: the amount by which spending exceeds income in a business or year
senses.definitionCN: 企业或年度中支出超过收入的金额
senses.example: The airline reported a loss for the third year running.
senses.exampleCN: 这家航空公司连续第三年报告亏损。
senses.why: Accounting reverses the idea of gain: what should have come back did not, and the shortfall is the loss.
senses.whyCN: 会计把收益的观念反过来：本该回来的没有回来，缺掉的那部分就是亏损。

senses.title: The death of someone close
senses.definition: the death of a relative or friend, experienced as bereavement
senses.definitionCN: 亲属或朋友的死亡，被视为丧亲之痛
senses.example: She took a long leave after the loss of her father.
senses.exampleCN: 父亲去世后，她请了很长的假。
senses.why: Death is the most absolute form of no longer having someone, so the word serves as its ordinary, gentle name.
senses.whyCN: 死亡是「不再拥有某人」最绝对的形式，因此这个词成了它平常而温和的说法。

senses.title: A decrease in amount or intensity
senses.definition: a reduction in quantity, energy or intensity as something escapes or fades
senses.definitionCN: 随着某物逸出或衰减，数量、能量或强度上的减少
senses.example: Insulation cut heat loss through the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 保温层减少了穿过墙壁的热量散失。
senses.why: Physics treats escaping heat as something that leaves the system, which is a loss to the system.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把逸出的热视为离开系统的某物，对系统而言就是损失。

senses.title: Failure to win a contest
senses.definition: a defeat in a game, election or contest
senses.definitionCN: 在比赛、选举或竞争中落败
senses.example: It was their third loss of the season.
senses.exampleCN: 这是他们本赛季的第三场失利。
senses.why: A defeat is the loss of a winning position, and sport shortened the phrase to the single word.
senses.whyCN: 失败就是失去获胜的位置，体育语境把这个短语缩短成一个词。

senses.title: An insured event or sum
senses.titleCN: 保险中的损失事件或金额
senses.definition: the damage or sum that an insurer agrees to cover under a policy
senses.definitionCN: 承保人依保单同意赔付的损害或金额
senses.example: The policy covered the loss of the cargo at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 保单承保了海上货物的损失。
senses.why: Insurance exists to price misfortune, so the word becomes a technical term for the event and its cost.
senses.whyCN: 保险的存在就是为不幸定价，因此这个词成了指事件及其代价的技术用语。

senses.title: The gap left by something valuable
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：珍贵之物消失后留下的空缺
senses.definition: the emptiness or deficit that remains after something valuable disappears
senses.definitionCN: 珍贵之物消失之后留下的空虚或欠缺
senses.example: The loss of trust was harder to repair than the loss of money.
senses.exampleCN: 信任的丧失比金钱的损失更难修补。
senses.why: Generalised, the word names any absence that registers as a deficit, whether the thing was money, heat, a person or trust.
senses.whyCN: 一般化之后，这个词指任何被感受为欠缺的缺席，无论所失之物是金钱、热量、人还是信任。

intro.en: Loss comes from Old English los 'loss, destruction', from a Germanic stem also seen in the verb lose; it has no Latin cognate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: loss 来自古英语 los「丧失、毁灭」，其日耳曼语词干也见于动词 lose；这个词没有拉丁同族词。年代为约数。

items.en: The noun goes back to a Germanic form meaning 'breaking up, loss', related to Old Norse los 'the breaking up of an army'.
items.cn: 这个名词可追溯到日耳曼语中表示「瓦解、丧失」的形式，与古诺尔斯语 los「军队溃散」相关。

items.en: Old English los meant 'loss, destruction, ruin', and the related verb losian meant 'to be lost, perish'.
items.cn: 古英语 los 意为「丧失、毁灭、毁坏」，相关动词 losian 意为「失踪、灭亡」。

items.en: In Middle English the noun settled into its modern spelling and the verb separated into lose, so the pair now differ in form and sound.
items.cn: 在中古英语中，名词固定为现代拼写，动词则分立为 lose，于是这对词在形与音上都分开了。

items.en: The commercial sense of a shortfall in the accounts developed in the sixteenth century alongside double-entry bookkeeping.
items.cn: 账目中出现缺口的商业义在十六世纪随复式记账一同发展。

items.en: Insurance made the word a term for a covered event, and sport made it a count of defeats; both usages spread in the modern period.
items.cn: 保险使这个词成为「承保事件」的术语，体育使它成为失败次数的计量；两种用法都在近代普及。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed, and the exact dates of the financial and insurance senses are not established.
items.cn: 来源不确定：更早的印欧词根属重构形式，财务义与保险义的确切年代亦未得到证明。

note.en: Group one holds the forms of the same Germanic stock, including one that drifted to a different meaning; group two holds words for damage, shortfall and defeat.
note.cn: 第一组同出日耳曼语词干，其中一个漂移到了别的意思；第二组指损害、缺口与失败。

entries.definition: To stop having something; the noun names the state, the verb names the event, and their spellings must not be swapped.
entries.definitionCN: 失去某物；名词指状态，动词指事件，两者的拼写不可混用。

entries.definition: The past participle and an adjective meaning missing or unable to find the way.
entries.definitionCN: 过去分词，也作形容词，意为丢失的或迷路的。

entries.definition: A person who loses, especially one who fails to win; it names a person, not an amount.
entries.definitionCN: 指失败的人，尤指未能获胜者；指人而非金额。

entries.definition: From the same Germanic root meaning 'free, loose', but it means 'not tight' and is not a synonym of loss.
entries.definitionCN: 同出表示「自由、松开」的日耳曼词根，但意为「不紧的」，并非 loss 的同义词。

entries.definition: Harm to a thing that reduces its value or usefulness; loss is the value that is gone.
entries.definitionCN: 对物品造成的损害，降低其价值或用途；loss 指已经失去的价值。

entries.definition: The amount by which something falls short, especially in public accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 某物不足的数额，尤指公共账目中的缺口。

entries.definition: A gradual decrease in amount or quality; it describes a process, while loss can be a single event.
entries.definitionCN: 数量或质量的逐渐下降；描述过程，而 loss 可以是一次事件。

entries.definition: The state of being beaten in a battle, game or election; it is narrower than loss.
entries.definitionCN: 在战斗、比赛或选举中被击败的状态；比 loss 更窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Germanic history, the real family and the real collocations.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的日耳曼语演变、真实词族与真实搭配。

normal.en: The old noun meant 'breaking up': something that was whole is now apart or gone.
normal.cn: 这个旧名词意为「瓦解」：原本完整的东西现在散开或消失了。

normal.en: The family runs lose, lost, loser, loss, lossless, lossy.
normal.cn: 词族包括 lose、lost、loser、loss、lossless、lossy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: at a loss, make a loss, cut losses, weight loss.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出各义：困惑或亏本、亏损、及时止损、体重下降。

normal.en: Loss is the state; lose is the event.
normal.cn: loss 是状态，lose 是事件。

normal.en: Accounting sets loss against profit, and sport sets it against a win.
normal.cn: 会计把亏损与利润相对，体育把失利与胜利相对。

abstract.en: Picture a drawer with one empty slot where something used to sit every day.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉，其中一个格子空了，那里原本每天都放着东西。

abstract.en: Picture a wall that lets warmth escape through it all winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙，整个冬天都让暖意从里面溜走。

abstract.en: Picture a column in a ledger that should have a number and has none.
abstract.cn: 想象账簿里一栏本该有数字，却空着。

examples.en: The loss of the harvest left the family short of cash.
examples.cn: 收成的损失让这家人现金短缺。

examples.en: Insurers estimate the loss before they settle the claim.
examples.cn: 承保人在理赔之前先估算损失。

examples.en: The team never recovered from that early loss.
examples.cn: 这支队伍始终没能从赛季初的那场失利中恢复过来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「落了（loss）就找不回」——东西掉了、钱亏了、人走了，都叫丧失

root: 古英语 los（丧失、毁灭），属日耳曼语源，与动词 lose 同出一系；更早的印欧词根属重构形式，无拉丁同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one absence: something that was there is no longer, and the word then names the thing missed, the money short, a death, an escaping quantity, a defeat, an insured event and finally any deficit at all.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个缺席展开：原本在那里的东西不在了；这个词再指被惋惜的对象、账上的缺款、死亡、逸出的量、一场失利、承保事件，最后指任何欠缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an empty place in a drawer where something used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽屉里一个原本放着东西的空位。

branches.en: ABSENCE: the event of losing and the thing whose absence is felt are two sides of one empty place.
branches.cn: 缺席：失去的事件与缺席被感受的对象，是同一个空位的两面。

branches.en: ACCOUNTS: the money that should have come back did not, and the gap is counted as a loss.
branches.cn: 账目：本该回来的钱没有回来，这个缺口就被计为亏损。

branches.en: DEATH: the most absolute absence gets the gentlest name.
branches.cn: 死亡：最绝对的缺席用了最温和的名称。

branches.en: MEASURED ABSENCE: escaping heat and insured cargo are both quantities that leave and must be priced.
branches.cn: 可量的缺席：逸出的热与承保的货物，都是离开并被定价的量。

branches.en: CONTEST AND GENERALITY: a defeat is the loss of a winning position, and any deficit repeats the same shape.
branches.cn: 竞争与泛化：失利是失去获胜位置，任何欠缺都重复同一形状。

intro.en: Loss is a native Germanic noun with no prefix and no Latin root; its ending marks a state rather than an act.
intro.cn: loss 是本族日耳曼名词，既无前缀也无拉丁词根；其词尾标记一种状态，而非一个动作。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor here; the Germanic noun los and the verb lose supply the whole family, so the Latin list is empty.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁语祖先；日耳曼名词 los 与动词 lose 提供整个词族，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.example: The old noun named a breaking apart.
items.exampleCN: 这个旧名词指「散开、瓦解」。

items.example: The verb and noun split in form.
items.exampleCN: 动词与名词在形式上分了家。

items.example: Losses are counted one by one.
items.exampleCN: 亏损是一笔一笔计数的。

items.meaning: the state of no longer having
items.example: The loss was never recovered.
items.exampleCN: 这项损失从未被挽回。

items.example: The lost keys turned up years later.
items.exampleCN: 丢失的钥匙多年后被找到。

items.example: The loser of the final took the prize money.
items.exampleCN: 决赛的失利者拿走了奖金。

items.example: The format is lossless.
items.exampleCN: 这种格式是无损的。

items.example: The file was compressed in a lossy way.
items.exampleCN: 这个文件以有损方式压缩。

definition_zh: 财务损失；金钱上的损失
definition_en: money lost through an event, a transaction or a period of operation
core_image: 一只账本摊在桌上，某一页的数字被红笔划掉，旁边写下一个更小的数
scene: 账本摊在桌上，某一页的数字被红笔划掉，旁边改写成更小的数。The flood caused a financial loss that the family could not absorb alone.
sceneCN: 账页上的数字被红笔划掉并改小，形成一笔亏空；句中的 financial loss 指「以金钱计量的损失」（第 1 个义项：因事件而失去的钱）。图中可辨识物件：账本、红笔、改写后的数字、计算器、保险单。

pos.zh: 财务损失；金钱上的损失

senses.title: Money lost in an event
senses.definition: money that is lost as the result of an accident, disaster or other event
senses.definitionCN: 因事故、灾害或其他事件而失去的钱
senses.example: The flood caused a financial loss that the family could not absorb alone.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水造成的财务损失，这家人无法独自承受。
senses.why: The phrase joins a measure to a misfortune: loss counted in money rather than in anything else.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把度量单位接到不幸上：损失以金钱而非其他东西来计量。

senses.title: An accounting loss
senses.definition: a negative result recorded in the accounts when costs exceed income
senses.definitionCN: 成本超过收入时记入账目的负数结果
senses.example: The audit revealed a financial loss hidden in the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 审计发现账目中隐藏着一笔财务亏损。
senses.why: Once loss is booked, it becomes a line in a statement, and the qualifier distinguishes it from other kinds of shortfall.
senses.whyCN: 一旦损失被入账，它就成了报表中的一行，而限定词把它与其他类型的缺口区分开。

senses.title: A capital loss on an investment
senses.definition: the amount by which an asset's value falls below what was paid for it
senses.definitionCN: 资产价值低于买入价的那部分金额
senses.example: They accepted a financial loss rather than hold the shares longer.
senses.exampleCN: 他们宁愿接受一笔财务损失，也不愿继续持有这些股票。
senses.why: Investing separates the price paid from the price realised, and the gap between them is counted as a loss.
senses.whyCN: 投资把买入价与实现价分开，两者之间的差距就被计为损失。

senses.title: An operating loss
senses.definition: a loss made by ordinary business activity before other gains or charges are counted
senses.definitionCN: 在计入其他收益或费用之前，由日常经营活动造成的亏损
senses.example: The retail division posted an operating financial loss.
senses.exampleCN: 零售部门录得经营亏损。
senses.why: Accounting separates trading from financing, so a loss from trading gets its own label.
senses.whyCN: 会计把经营与融资分开，因此来自经营的亏损得到自己的标签。

senses.title: A loss covered by insurance
senses.definition: a loss that an insurer agrees to pay for under the terms of a policy
senses.definitionCN: 承保人依保单条款同意赔付的损失
senses.example: The policy covers financial loss from business interruption.
senses.exampleCN: 该保单承保营业中断造成的财务损失。
senses.why: Insurance needs to name the kind of harm it covers, and money lost is one standard category.
senses.whyCN: 保险需要指明承保的是哪类损害，而金钱损失是其中一个标准类别。

senses.title: A loss to the wider economy
senses.definition: the value destroyed in an economy by a shock, measured in money
senses.definitionCN: 冲击给一个经济体造成的、以金钱计量的价值毁损
senses.example: Economists put the financial loss from the port closure in the billions.
senses.exampleCN: 经济学家估计港口关闭造成的财务损失达数十亿。
senses.why: At the scale of a country, many private losses are added into one public figure.
senses.whyCN: 到了国家尺度，许多私人损失被加总成一个公共数字。

senses.title: A reported loss in statements
senses.titleCN: 财务报表中报告的亏损
senses.definition: the loss figure that a company discloses in its published statements
senses.definitionCN: 公司在公开报表中披露的亏损数字
senses.example: The annual report disclosed a financial loss for the second year.
senses.exampleCN: 年报披露了第二年的财务亏损。
senses.why: Disclosure has its own vocabulary, and the phrase marks a figure that has passed audit and been made public.
senses.whyCN: 披露有其自身词汇，这个短语标记一个经过审计并向公众公布的数字。

senses.title: Any loss measured in money
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：任何以金钱计量的损失
senses.definition: any deprivation whose size is expressed in money, including lost opportunity or reputation
senses.definitionCN: 规模以金钱表示的任何损失，包括机会或声誉的损失
senses.example: The reputational damage was counted as a financial loss.
senses.exampleCN: 声誉损害被折算成一笔财务损失。
senses.why: The phrase can price what is not itself money, so long as a money value can be put on it.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语可以给本身并非金钱的东西定价，只要能为它估出一个金钱价值。

intro.en: The phrase joins financial, from Latin finis 'end, boundary' through French finance, with loss, an Old English noun of Germanic origin. The compound belongs to modern accounting and insurance. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语由 financial 与 loss 组成：前者经法语 finance 来自拉丁语 finis「终点、边界」；后者是日耳曼语源的古英语名词。复合短语属于近代会计与保险。年代为约数。

items.en: Finis meant 'end, boundary, limit'. A debt was settled when it reached its end, and that idea produced the money sense of the French word.
items.cn: finis 意为「终点、边界、限度」。债务到达终点即为结清，这一观念产生了法语词的金钱义。

items.en: Old French finance meant 'payment, debt, settlement', from the verb finer 'to settle, pay'.
items.cn: 古法语 finance 意为「付款、债务、结清」，来自动词 finer「结清、支付」。

items.en: English borrowed finance in the fifteenth century; its modern sense of money management and public revenue took shape in the eighteenth.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 finance；其「资金管理、公共收入」的现代义在十八世纪成形。

items.en: Loss goes back to Old English los 'loss, destruction', from a Germanic stem; it has no connection with the Latin word for an end.
items.cn: loss 可追溯到古英语 los「丧失、毁灭」，出自日耳曼语词干；它与拉丁语中表示「终点」的词毫无关联。

items.en: Financial loss appears in nineteenth- and twentieth-century insurance, accounting and economics, wherever a misfortune must be given a money value.
items.cn: financial loss 出现在十九、二十世纪的保险、会计与经济学中，凡需为不幸估出金钱价值之处都用它。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first use of the exact phrase is not recorded precisely, and the deeper root of the Germanic noun behind loss is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个确切短语的首见记录无法精确定位，loss 背后那个日耳曼名词的更早词根属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the two halves and their forms, which are easy to confuse; group two holds other ways of naming a money shortfall.
note.cn: 第一组是短语的两半及其形式，容易混淆；第二组是其他指金钱缺口的说法。

entries.definition: Means 'of money or finance'; it needs a noun such as loss, year or adviser to complete it.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「金钱或金融的」；必须搭配一个名词（如损失、年度、顾问）才完整。

entries.definition: Either the management of money or the act of providing funds; it is not the shortfall itself.
entries.definitionCN: 或指资金管理，或指提供资金的行为；它不是缺口本身。

entries.definition: Modifies a verb or adjective, as in financially dependent; it cannot stand where a noun is required.
entries.definitionCN: 修饰动词或形容词，如「经济上依赖」；不能占据名词的位置。

entries.definition: The loss on its own may be emotional or physical; the qualifier limits it to money.
entries.definitionCN: 单独使用时，损失可能是情感或身体上的；限定词把它限定为金钱。

entries.definition: A loss on the sale or valuation of an asset; it is one species of financial loss.
entries.definitionCN: 资产出售或估值上的损失；是财务损失的一个种类。

entries.definition: Loss measured in economic value, including lost output and welfare, not only cash.
entries.definitionCN: 以经济价值计量的损失，包括产出与福利的损失，不限于现金。

entries.definition: The gap between what is available and what is required, common in public budgets.
entries.definitionCN: 可用量与所需量之间的缺口，常见于公共预算。

entries.definition: Physical harm to property or reputation; it may or may not be given a money value.
entries.definitionCN: 对财产或声誉的实际损害；未必被折算成金钱。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real two halves, the real money vocabulary and the real insurance phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的两半、真实的金钱词汇与真实的保险搭配。

normal.en: Finance once meant settling a debt at its end; loss means the amount that never came back.
normal.cn: 金融一词曾指在终点结清债务；损失则是那笔始终没回来的钱。

normal.en: The family runs finance, financial, financially, financier, loss, lose.
normal.cn: 词族包括 finance、financial、financially、financier、loss、lose。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the context: suffer a financial loss, cover a financial loss, financial loss insurance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出语境：遭受财务损失、弥补财务损失、财务损失保险。

normal.en: The adjective does not change the noun: financial loss is loss priced in money.
normal.cn: 形容词并不改变名词：财务损失就是以金钱定价的损失。

normal.en: Insurance turns a misfortune into a figure, which is exactly what this phrase names.
normal.cn: 保险把不幸变成一个数字，而这正是这个短语所指。

abstract.en: Picture a number crossed out and replaced by a smaller one in red ink.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字被划掉，旁边用红笔写上一个更小的数。

abstract.en: Picture a wallet that is lighter at the end of the month than at the start.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱包，月底比月初轻。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger with one column that will never balance.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账簿，其中一栏永远无法平衡。

examples.en: The port strike caused a financial loss for exporters.
examples.cn: 港口罢工给出口商造成财务损失。

examples.en: Small firms often cannot survive a large financial loss.
examples.cn: 小公司往往经不起一次重大财务损失。

examples.en: The insurer disputed the size of the financial loss.
examples.cn: 承保人对财务损失的规模提出异议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「financial（钱的）＋loss（丢了）」——钱包里丢掉的那部分，就是财务损失

root: financial 经法语 finance 来自拉丁语 finis（终点、边界），原指债务结清；loss 为古英语 los（丧失），属日耳曼语源。二者组合指以金钱计量的损失。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one figure: a misfortune is converted into money, and that figure is then read as an event's cost, a booked loss, a fall in asset value, a trading result, an insured item, a national total, a disclosed number and finally any deprivation with a price tag.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个数字展开：不幸被换算成钱；这个数字再被读成事件的代价、入账的亏损、资产价值下跌、经营结果、承保项目、全国总额、披露的数字，最后指任何带价签的损失。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure crossed out and replaced by a smaller one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个数字被划掉，换成一个更小的数。

branches.en: EVENT AND BOOK: a misfortune becomes money, then a line in the accounts.
branches.cn: 事件与账簿：不幸先变成钱，再变成账目中的一行。

branches.en: INVESTMENT AND TRADING: a fall in asset value and a trading shortfall are two ways the same gap appears.
branches.cn: 投资与经营：资产价值下跌与经营缺口，是同一个缺口出现的两种方式。

branches.en: INSURANCE: the covered loss is the misfortune given a contractual price.
branches.cn: 保险：被承保的损失，就是被合同定价的不幸。

branches.en: SCALE AND DISCLOSURE: private losses add into a national total, and audited figures are published.
branches.cn: 规模与披露：私人损失加总成全国数字，经审计的数字则被公布。

branches.en: PRICE TAG: even reputation and opportunity can be converted into this figure.
branches.cn: 价签：连声誉与机会都可以被换算成这个数字。

intro.en: The phrase pairs a Latin-derived adjective of money with a Germanic noun of loss, so its two halves come from different language stocks.
intro.cn: 这个短语把源自拉丁语、表示金钱的形容词，与日耳曼语源的「丧失」名词配在一起，两半来自不同的语源。

latinIntro.en: Latin finis supplies the finance half; the loss half has no Latin ancestor and comes from Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 finis 提供「金融」那一半；「损失」那一半没有拉丁语祖先，来自古英语。

items.example: A debt ends when it is settled.
items.exampleCN: 债务在结清时到达终点。

items.meaning: to end a debt by paying
items.example: Settlement gave the word its money sense.
items.exampleCN: 结清这一动作赋予该词金钱义。

items.example: Finance became a field of its own.
items.exampleCN: 金融成为独立领域。

items.example: Financial records must be kept.
items.exampleCN: 财务记录必须保存。

items.example: The project is financially sound.
items.exampleCN: 这个项目在财务上是稳健的。

items.example: The financier backed the railway.
items.exampleCN: 这位金融家资助了铁路。

items.example: The Germanic noun carried the sense of loss.
items.exampleCN: 这个日耳曼名词承载了「丧失」之义。

items.meaning: the state of no longer having
items.example: The loss was recorded at once.
items.exampleCN: 损失被立即记录。

items.example: The firm reported a financial loss.
items.exampleCN: 该公司报告了财务损失。

definition_zh: 投资；投资额；投入（时间、精力）；被投资的对象
definition_en: the act of putting money, time or effort into something in order to gain a return later
core_image: 一粒种子被埋进土里，地面上只插着一根小木牌，牌上写着日期
scene: 一粒种子被埋进土里，地面只插着一根写有日期的小木牌，收获要在很久以后。Her investment in the vineyard took eight years to pay off.
sceneCN: 种子埋下时看不到回报，只在木牌上记下日期；句中的 investment 指「为日后回报而投入的钱或资源」（第 1 个义项：为获取未来收益而投入资金）。图中可辨识物件：埋种子的土坑、木牌、铁锹、账本、幼苗。

pos.zh: 投资；投资额；投入；被投资对象

senses.title: Money put in to earn a return
senses.titleCN: 为获取回报而投入的钱
senses.definition: the act of putting money into an asset, project or business in order to earn income or profit later
senses.definitionCN: 把钱投入资产、项目或企业，以便日后获得收入或利润的行为
senses.example: Her investment in the vineyard took eight years to pay off.
senses.exampleCN: 她在葡萄园上的投资用了八年才回本。
senses.why: The noun names the act of dressing money in a new form, which is the picture behind the Latin verb.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指给钱「换上一件新衣」的动作，这正是拉丁动词背后的意象。

senses.title: The sum of money put in
senses.definition: the amount of money committed to an asset or project
senses.definitionCN: 投入到某项资产或项目中的金额
senses.example: The fund attracted an investment of several million.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金吸引了一笔数百万的投资。
senses.why: As with many action nouns, the same word can name the deed and the sum it involves.
senses.whyCN: 像许多动作名词一样，同一个词既可指行为，也可指行为涉及的金额。

senses.title: A thing worth putting money into
senses.definition: an asset or property bought as a way of storing and growing value
senses.definitionCN: 为保值增值而购置的资产或房产
senses.example: The flat was bought as an investment, not a home.
senses.exampleCN: 这套公寓是作为投资品而非住所买下的。
senses.why: Once the act is familiar, the object of the act can take the same name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种行为变得常见，行为的对象也可以使用同一个名称。

senses.title: Time or effort devoted to a future gain
senses.definition: time, effort or emotion given to something in the expectation of a later benefit
senses.definitionCN: 为期待日后好处而给予某事的时间、精力或情感
senses.example: Learning the language was a long-term investment in her career.
senses.exampleCN: 学习这门语言是对她职业生涯的长期投入。
senses.why: If money can be invested, so can any limited resource whose return arrives later.
senses.whyCN: 既然钱可以投资，任何回报较晚到达的有限资源也都可以投资。

senses.title: Capital spending in an economy
senses.definition: spending by firms or states on machines, buildings and infrastructure
senses.definitionCN: 企业或国家在机器、建筑与基础设施上的支出
senses.example: Public investment in rail has lagged for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路方面的公共投资已落后了十年。
senses.why: Macroeconomics treats such spending as a flow that adds to the capital stock, hence investment rather than cost.
senses.whyCN: 宏观经济学把这类支出视为增加资本存量的流量，因此称之为投资而非成本。

senses.title: A portfolio or strategy decision
senses.definition: the selection and management of assets held in order to balance risk and return
senses.definitionCN: 为平衡风险与回报而持有并管理资产的选择
senses.example: The board reviewed its investment in emerging markets.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会审视了其在新兴市场的投资。
senses.why: Modern finance makes investment a managed category rather than a single purchase.
senses.whyCN: 现代金融使投资成为一个被管理的类别，而不只是一次购买。

senses.title: The historical sense of a siege
senses.definition: the act of surrounding a town or fortress with troops in order to capture it
senses.definitionCN: 用军队包围城镇或要塞以图攻取的行为
senses.example: The chronicle describes the investment of the castle.
senses.exampleCN: 这部编年史描述了那座城堡的围困。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant 'to clothe or surround', and a besieging army literally wraps a place around.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「穿衣、包围」，而围城的军队正是把一个地方从四周裹住。

senses.title: Any commitment repaid later
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：日后才有回报的任何投入
senses.definition: any cost accepted now in the expectation that something larger will come back later
senses.definitionCN: 为期待日后有更大回报而于现在承受的任何代价
senses.example: Patience is an investment that pays in ways no ledger records.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是一种以账本无法记录的方式回报的投入。
senses.why: At its most general the word is a bargain with time: give up something now, receive more later.
senses.whyCN: 在最一般的意义上，这个词是与时间做的一笔交易：现在放弃一些，日后收回更多。

intro.en: Investment is the noun of invest, from Latin investire 'to clothe, surround', built on in- 'in' and vestire 'to clothe'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: investment 是动词 invest 的名词；invest 来自拉丁语 investire「穿衣、包围」，由表「进入」的前缀与 vestire「穿衣」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Vestis meant 'garment, clothing'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the suggestions sometimes made are not established.
items.cn: vestis 意为「衣服、衣着」。其更早来源不确定；偶有提出的联系未得到证明。

items.en: Vestire meant 'to clothe, to dress', and it also supplied the vocabulary of putting on a role or a quality.
items.cn: vestire 意为「给……穿衣」，也用于表示「披上某种角色或性质」。

items.en: In- 'in' plus vestire produced investire, 'to clothe, to surround', used of dressing someone and of encircling a place.
items.cn: 表「进入」的前缀加 vestire 构成 investire「穿衣、包围」，既用于为人着衣，也用于围住一个地方。

items.en: Medieval and early modern English used invest for granting an office or rank and for the surrounding of a town by troops.
items.cn: 中古及近代早期英语用 invest 表示授予职位或爵位，也指军队围住城镇。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the word was applied to putting money into a venture, and by the nineteenth century investment was a standard term of industry and finance.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个词被用于把钱投入一项事业；到十九世纪，investment 已成为工业与金融的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first date of the money sense is not settled, and the origin of vestis before Latin is unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：金钱义的确切首见年代没有定论，vestis 在拉丁语之前的来源不明。

note.en: Group one holds the same investing family, where grammar makes the difference; group two holds other ways of putting money to work.
note.cn: 第一组同属「投资」词族，差别在语法；第二组是其他把钱投入使用的方式。

entries.definition: To put money or effort in; the noun names the act or the sum.
entries.definitionCN: 投入金钱或精力；名词指行为或金额。

entries.definition: The person who invests; it cannot name the money or the project.
entries.definitionCN: 进行投资的人；不能指钱或项目。

entries.definition: The activity as a process; investment is the act completed or the thing held.
entries.definitionCN: 作为过程的活动；investment 是完成的行为或持有的对象。

entries.definition: The sale or withdrawal of assets; it is built from the same clothing image with a prefix of separation.
entries.definitionCN: 出售或撤出资产；由同一个「穿衣」意象加表分离的前缀构成。

entries.definition: Money supplied for a project, often by a donor or a state; it stresses the source rather than the expected return.
entries.definitionCN: 为项目提供的钱，常来自捐赠者或国家；强调来源而非预期回报。

entries.definition: The accumulated money and assets used to produce more; investment is the flow that adds to it.
entries.definitionCN: 用于再生产而积累的资金与资产；投资是使它增加的流量。

entries.definition: A share or interest held in a business; it is one possible result of an investment.
entries.definitionCN: 在一家企业中持有的股份或权益；是投资的一种可能结果。

entries.definition: Buying assets in the hope of a quick price gain; it takes more risk than investment is usually understood to take.
entries.definitionCN: 为求价格快速上涨而买入资产；承担的风险通常高于一般所说的投资。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real clothing image, the real family and the real finance phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「穿衣」意象、真实词族与真实金融搭配。

normal.en: To invest was to clothe: money is dressed in a new form and must wait to be seen again.
normal.cn: 投资原本是「穿衣」：钱被换上一件新衣，要等很久才能再被看见。

normal.en: The family runs invest, investment, investor, investable, reinvestment.
normal.cn: 词族包括 invest、investment、investor、investable、reinvestment。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: foreign investment, capital investment, return on investment.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：外国投资、资本投资、投资回报率。

normal.en: The old siege sense survives in histories: the investment of a castle.
normal.cn: 古老的围困义仍存于史书：对一座城堡的围困。

normal.en: Investment is the act or the thing; investing is the ongoing activity.
normal.cn: investment 是行为或对象；investing 是持续进行的活动。

abstract.en: Picture a seed buried under a small wooden marker with a date on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子被埋在一根写着日期的小木牌下。

abstract.en: Picture a coat put on a coin so that it can travel through winter.
abstract.cn: 想象给一枚硬币穿上外套，让它能穿过冬天。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge built now that nobody will cross for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一座现在建好、却多年无人走过的桥。

examples.en: The factory's investment in cleaner equipment paid for itself.
examples.cn: 工厂在更清洁设备上的投资收回了成本。

examples.en: Foreign investment brought new jobs but also new risks.
examples.cn: 外国投资带来了新工作，也带来了新风险。

examples.en: She treated the language course as an investment in herself.
examples.cn: 她把这门语言课程当作对自己的投资。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（进去）＋vest（马甲）」——把钱穿上一件马甲放进项目里，等它日后长回来

root: 拉丁语 investire（穿衣、包围）＝in-（进入）＋vestire（穿衣），源自 vestis（衣服）；金钱义自十七世纪起发展，investment 十九世纪成为标准术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one bargain: something valuable is given a new form and left to grow, and the word then names the sum, the thing bought, time and effort, capital spending, a managed portfolio, an old siege and finally any cost accepted for a later return.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一笔交易展开：有价值之物被换上新形、留在那里生长；这个词再指金额、买下的对象、时间与精力、资本支出、被管理的组合、古老的围城，最后指任何为日后回报而承受的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: money dressed in a new form and left to grow.
core.cn: 核心意象：钱被换上新装，留在那里生长。

branches.en: ACT AND SUM: the deed of committing money and the money committed are one event seen twice.
branches.cn: 行为与金额：投入钱的动作与被投入的钱，是同一件事的两种看法。

branches.en: OBJECT: what is bought to hold value takes the name of the act.
branches.cn: 对象：为保值而买下的东西，承接了行为的名称。

branches.en: OTHER RESOURCES: time and effort can be dressed and left to grow just as money can.
branches.cn: 其他资源：时间与精力也能像钱一样被换上新装、留在那里生长。

branches.en: SCALE: capital spending adds to a national stock, and a portfolio turns investment into a managed category.
branches.cn: 尺度：资本支出增加国家存量，投资组合则把投资变成被管理的类别。

branches.en: OLD IMAGE AND GENERAL FORM: the besieging army wraps a town, and any deferred gain repeats the shape.
branches.cn: 旧意象与一般形式：围城军队从四周裹住城镇，任何延迟的回报都重复这一形状。

intro.en: The word is a prefix of entry plus a verb of clothing, with a noun suffix that marks the act or its result.
intro.cn: 这个词由表「进入」的前缀、表「穿衣」的动词，以及标记行为或结果的名词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis and vestire supply the root; the prefix turns dressing into wrapping something around.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis 与 vestire 提供词根；前缀把「穿衣」变成「从外面裹住」。

items.example: The prefix puts the garment on the body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把衣服穿到身体上。

items.example: The noun names what is put on.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指被穿上之物。

items.example: The verb gives the act of dressing.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出「穿衣」的动作。

items.example: The compound can wrap a person or a town.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词可以裹住一个人，也可以围住一座城。

items.example: They invest in new machinery.
items.exampleCN: 他们投资于新机器。

items.example: The investment matured after ten years.
items.exampleCN: 这项投资十年后到期。

items.example: Investors demanded clearer accounts.
items.exampleCN: 投资者要求更清晰的账目。

items.example: The region is seen as investable.
items.exampleCN: 该地区被视为可供投资。

items.example: Reinvestment delayed the payout.
items.exampleCN: 再投资推迟了分红。

definition_zh: 投资；投入（时间、精力）；授予（权力、职位）；包围
definition_en: to put money, time or effort into something for a later return, or formally to give someone a power or office
core_image: 一个人把一叠钱放进一只标着年份的盒子，盒子被推到架子深处
scene: 一个人把一叠钱放进标着年份的盒子，再把盒子推到架子深处。They decided to invest in a smaller, more efficient furnace.
sceneCN: 钱被放进标着年份的盒子，推到架子深处等待；句中的 invest 指「为日后回报而投入资金」（第 1 个义项：把钱投入资产或项目）。图中可辨识物件：木盒、年份标签、钱叠、架子、账本。

senses.title: Put money in for a return
senses.titleCN: 为获取回报而投入资金
senses.definition: to put money into an asset, project or business in the hope of earning more later
senses.definitionCN: 把钱投入资产、项目或企业，期望日后赚回更多
senses.example: They decided to invest in a smaller, more efficient furnace.
senses.exampleCN: 他们决定投资一台更小、更高效的炉子。
senses.why: The core sense dresses money in a productive form and leaves it there until it yields.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是给钱换上一件能生产的形态，把它留在那里直到产出。

senses.title: Supply capital to a company
senses.definition: to provide a company with capital in exchange for a share of ownership or future profit
senses.definitionCN: 向公司提供资本，以换取部分所有权或未来利润
senses.example: A group of doctors invested in the new clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 一群医生投资了这家新诊所。
senses.why: The act usually has a counterparty, and the money becomes the company's capital rather than the investor's cash.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作通常有对手方，钱于是变成公司的资本，而不再是投资者的现金。

senses.title: Devote time or energy
senses.definition: to give time, effort or care to something because a later benefit is expected
senses.definitionCN: 为期待日后好处而把时间、精力或心力给予某事
senses.example: She invested years in learning the trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她投入多年学习这门手艺。
senses.why: Once the money sense is established, any limited resource can be described as invested.
senses.whyCN: 金钱义一旦确立，任何有限的资源都可以被说成是「投入」的。

senses.title: Give someone a formal office
senses.definition: to install someone formally in an office, rank or right, often with a ceremony
senses.definitionCN: 以仪式正式把某人安置于职位、爵位或权利之中
senses.example: The new bishop was invested with the symbols of office.
senses.exampleCN: 新主教被授予职位的象征物。
senses.why: The oldest sense is clothing: the person is dressed in the visible marks of a role.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意义是穿衣：人被披上某个角色的可见标志。

senses.title: Buy assets for future income
senses.definition: to buy shares, property or other assets in order to receive income or a capital gain
senses.definitionCN: 为获得收入或资本增值而购买股票、房产等资产
senses.example: He invested in bonds rather than in shares.
senses.exampleCN: 他投资债券而非股票。
senses.why: This is the everyday finance sense: a purchase made for what it will produce, not for what it is.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常金融义：购买不是为了东西本身，而是为了它将产出什么。

senses.title: Surround a place with troops
senses.definition: to surround a town or fortress with armed forces in order to capture it
senses.definitionCN: 用武装力量包围城镇或要塞以图攻取
senses.example: The army invested the fortress before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 军队在黎明前包围了要塞。
senses.why: The Latin verb's other literal sense was to wrap around, and a siege wraps a place in soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词的另一个字面义是「从四周裹住」，而围城就是用士兵把地方裹起来。

senses.title: Bestow a quality or right
senses.definition: to grant a quality, power or right to something in a formal or literary way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式或书面方式把某种性质、权力或权利给予某物
senses.example: The charter invested the town with the right to hold a market.
senses.exampleCN: 特许状授予该镇举办集市的权利。
senses.why: From clothing a person, the verb widens to clothing a thing with an attribute.
senses.whyCN: 从给人穿衣出发，这个动词扩展到给事物披上某种属性。

senses.title: Accept a cost for a later payoff
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：为日后收益先承担代价
senses.definition: to accept a cost, risk or delay now because a larger benefit is expected later
senses.definitionCN: 因预期日后有更大好处而于现在承受代价、风险或延迟
senses.example: They invested patience in the negotiations, not money.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在谈判中投入的是耐心，而不是金钱。
senses.why: At its most general, to invest is to make a deliberate trade with time.
senses.whyCN: 在最一般的意义上，「投资」就是与时间有意做成一笔交易。

intro.en: Invest comes from Latin investire 'to clothe, surround', from in- 'in' and vestire 'to clothe'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: invest 来自拉丁语 investire「穿衣、包围」，由表「进入」的前缀与 vestire「穿衣」构成。年代为约数。

items.en: Vestis meant 'garment'. Its origin before Latin is uncertain; no reliable deeper root can be stated.
items.cn: vestis 意为「衣服」。它在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，无法给出可靠的更早词根。

items.en: Vestire meant 'to clothe or dress', and could also mean to put on a quality or role.
items.cn: vestire 意为「给……穿衣」，也可指披上某种性质或角色。

items.en: In- 'in' plus vestire gave investire, 'to clothe, to surround'. Both the dressing and the encircling senses are literal in Latin.
items.cn: 表「进入」的前缀加 vestire 构成 investire「穿衣、包围」。着衣与环绕这两个意义在拉丁语中都是字面的。

items.en: English used invest for the ceremony of granting an office, and histories used it for the surrounding of a town.
items.cn: 英语用 invest 指授予职位的仪式，史书则用它指围住城镇。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the verb was applied to committing money to a venture, and the usage dominated by the nineteenth.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个动词被用于把钱投入一项事业，到十九世纪已成为主导用法。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of the financial sense is not pinned down, and the origin of vestis is unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：金钱义的首见年代无法精确定位，vestis 的来源亦不明。

note.en: Group one holds forms from the same clothing verb, including one built with a prefix of separation; group two holds verbs of supplying money.
note.cn: 第一组同出「穿衣」这一动词，其中一个带表分离的前缀；第二组是提供金钱的动词。

entries.definition: The act or the money put in; the verb cannot stand as the subject of 'was large'.
entries.definitionCN: 指行为或投入的钱；动词不能充当「数额很大」的主语。

entries.definition: The person who invests; it is not the act and not the asset.
entries.definitionCN: 进行投资的人；既不是行为，也不是资产。

entries.definition: To sell off or strip away assets, built with a prefix of separation on the same clothing root.
entries.definitionCN: 出售或剥离资产，由同一个「穿衣」词根加表分离的前缀构成。

entries.definition: A garment, or as a verb to give a right to someone; it shares the root but not the financial sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指背心，作动词则指把权利授予某人；同根，但不含投资义。

entries.definition: To provide the money for a project; the emphasis is on supply, not on the expected return.
entries.definitionCN: 为项目提供资金；重点在供给，而非预期回报。

entries.definition: To find or arrange the money for something, often a purchase or a public scheme.
entries.definitionCN: 为某事筹措资金，常指一次采购或公共计划。

entries.definition: To buy assets hoping for a quick price rise; it implies more risk than invest usually does.
entries.definitionCN: 为求价格快速上涨而买入资产；暗示的风险高于一般的投资。

entries.definition: To give money or property permanently to an institution, or to give a quality to someone.
entries.definitionCN: 永久性地把钱或财产赠予机构，或把某种品质赋予某人。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real clothing image, the real family and the real phrases of money and office.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「穿衣」意象、真实词族，以及金钱与职位的真实搭配。

normal.en: The core image is dressing: money is dressed in a productive form, a person in the robes of office.
normal.cn: 核心意象是穿衣：钱被披上能生产的形态，人被披上职位的袍服。

normal.en: The family runs invest, investment, investor, investable, reinvest, divest.
normal.cn: 词族包括 invest、investment、investor、investable、reinvest、divest。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the money sense: invest in, invest heavily, invest capital, invest time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金钱义：投资于、大举投资、投入资本、投入时间。

normal.en: The office sense survives in ceremonial language: a bishop is invested with authority.
normal.cn: 职位义存于仪式语言：主教被授予权柄。

normal.en: The siege sense survives in histories: an army invests a fortress.
normal.cn: 围困义存于史书：军队包围一座要塞。

abstract.en: Picture a coin wearing a coat and waiting out a long winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币穿着外套，等过漫长的冬天。

abstract.en: Picture a person dressed in clothes that are too heavy for the work they must do.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人被穿上过于厚重的衣服，却还要去做那件工作。

abstract.en: Picture a wall of soldiers closing around a town like a coat around a body.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈士兵围住城镇，像外套裹住身体。

examples.en: The city plans to invest in flood defences next year.
examples.cn: 该市计划明年投资防洪设施。

examples.en: He invested his savings in a small bookshop.
examples.cn: 他把积蓄投入了一家小书店。

examples.en: Good teachers invest time in the slowest learners.
examples.cn: 好老师会把时间投入学得最慢的学生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in（往里）＋vest（马甲）」——把钱穿上马甲放进项目，等它日后长回来

root: 拉丁语 investire（穿衣、包围）＝in-（进入）＋vestire（穿衣），源自 vestis（衣服）；授予职位义为最古老用法，金钱义十七世纪起发展。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: something is dressed in a new form and left in place, and the gesture then covers money, company capital, time, an office ceremony, asset purchases, a besieging army, a granted right and finally any cost accepted for a later return.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：给某物换上新装并留在原处；这个动作再依次覆盖金钱、企业资本、时间、授职仪式、资产购置、围城军队、授予的权利，最后指任何为日后回报而承受的代价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something dressed in a new form and left to wait.
core.cn: 核心意象：某物被换上新装，留在那里等待。

branches.en: MONEY: buying an asset is the everyday form of dressing money for later gain.
branches.cn: 金钱：购置资产是给钱换装、等待日后增益的日常形式。

branches.en: COMPANY: the committed money becomes another firm's capital.
branches.cn: 企业：投入的钱变成另一家企业的资本。

branches.en: OTHER RESOURCES: time and attention can be dressed and left to grow.
branches.cn: 其他资源：时间与注意力也能被换上新装、留在那里生长。

branches.en: FORMAL DRESSING: a person is installed in office, and a thing can be clothed with a right.
branches.cn: 正式着装：人被打扮安置进职位，事物也能被披上一项权利。

branches.en: OLD AND GENERAL: the besieging army literally wraps a place, and any deferred gain repeats the gesture.
branches.cn: 旧义与泛义：围城军队字面上裹住一个地方，任何延迟的回报都重复这个动作。

intro.en: The verb is a prefix of entry plus a verb of clothing, and the same two pieces build the nouns around it.
intro.cn: 这个动词由表「进入」的前缀加表「穿衣」的动词构成，同样的两部分也构成它周围的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vestis and vestire supply the root, and the prefix marks putting something into or onto.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 vestis 与 vestire 提供词根，前缀标出「放入、穿上」的方向。

items.example: The prefix puts the garment on.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把衣服穿上去。

items.example: The noun supplies the clothing image.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供穿衣的意象。

items.example: The verb gives the act.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词给出动作。

items.example: The compound covers both senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词涵盖两种意义。

items.example: They invest in research.
items.exampleCN: 他们投资于研究。

items.example: The investment was slow to mature.
items.exampleCN: 这项投资成熟得很慢。

items.example: The investor took a seat on the board.
items.exampleCN: 这位投资者获得了董事会席位。

items.example: They reinvested the profit.
items.exampleCN: 他们把利润再投资。

items.example: The group divested its older plants.
items.exampleCN: 该集团剥离了较旧的工厂。

definition_en: a person or organisation that puts money into an asset, project or company expecting a return
core_image: 长桌一侧坐着几位出资人，对面是拿着计划书的创业者，桌上摊着股权表
scene: 长桌两侧各坐一排人，中间摊着股权表与计划书，气氛谨慎。An investor from the coast agreed to fund the first year of the studio.
sceneCN: 出资人与创业者隔桌相对，桌上摆着股权表；句中的 investor 指「把钱投入项目以期待回报的人或机构」（第 1 个义项：投入资金的一方）。图中可辨识物件：长桌、股权表、计划书、钢笔、茶杯。

senses.title: A person who puts money into assets
senses.definition: a person who commits money to shares, property or another asset in order to earn a return
senses.definitionCN: 为获得回报而把钱投入股票、房产或其他资产的人
senses.example: An investor from the coast agreed to fund the first year of the studio.
senses.exampleCN: 一位来自沿海的投资者同意资助这家工作室的第一年。
senses.why: The agent noun names the person who performs the act of dressing money in a productive form.
senses.whyCN: 这个施动名词指执行「给钱换上有生产力的形态」这一动作的人。

senses.title: An institution that invests
senses.definition: a pension fund, insurer, bank or fund manager that invests on behalf of others
senses.definitionCN: 代表他人进行投资的养老基金、保险机构、银行或基金管理人
senses.example: An institutional investor bought most of the new shares.
senses.exampleCN: 一家机构投资者买下了大部分新股。
senses.why: When investing is done at scale by organisations, the person noun extends to the body that acts like a person.
senses.whyCN: 当投资由组织大规模进行时，指人的名词也扩展到像人一样行动的组织。

senses.title: An early backer of a new venture
senses.definition: a private individual who provides early capital to a young company, often in exchange for shares
senses.definitionCN: 向年轻公司提供早期资本的私人个体，通常以换取股份为条件
senses.example: An angel investor paid for the first prototype.
senses.exampleCN: 一位天使投资人出资做了第一个样机。
senses.why: Fixed phrases split the role by stage and by risk, and the earliest stage acquires a vivid name of its own.
senses.whyCN: 固定搭配按阶段与风险切分角色，最早的阶段得到了一个生动的名称。

senses.title: An investor from another country
senses.definition: a person or fund that puts money into assets in a country other than its own
senses.definitionCN: 把资金投入本国以外资产的个人或基金
senses.example: Foreign investors were slow to return after the crisis.
senses.exampleCN: 危机之后，外国投资者迟迟没有回来。
senses.why: Capital crosses borders, so the word is qualified by nationality to mark where the money comes from.
senses.whyCN: 资本会跨越国界，因此这个词常用国别限定，以标明资金来自何处。

senses.title: A holder of shares
senses.definition: a person who owns shares in a company and therefore holds a claim on its profits
senses.definitionCN: 拥有公司股份、因而对其利润享有索取权的人
senses.example: Small investors rarely attend the annual meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 小股东很少出席年度会议。
senses.why: Owning a share is one result of investing, so the word can stand for the resulting ownership.
senses.whyCN: 持有股份是投资的一种结果，因此这个词也可指由此形成的所有权身份。

senses.title: A provider of capital to a business
senses.titleCN: 为企业提供资本的一方
senses.definition: a person or body that supplies money to a business, whether as shares, loans or both
senses.definitionCN: 为企业提供资金的人或机构，形式可以是股份、贷款或两者兼有
senses.example: The founders spent a month looking for a patient investor.
senses.exampleCN: 创始人花了一个月寻找有耐心的出资人。
senses.why: From the company's side, the investor is the source of funds, which is why the word appears in pitches and deals.
senses.whyCN: 从企业角度看，投资者就是资金来源，因此这个词出现在路演与交易中。

senses.title: One who invests time or effort
senses.definition: a person who gives time, effort or trust to something expecting a later benefit
senses.definitionCN: 为期待日后好处而给予某物时间、精力或信任的人
senses.example: Parents are investors of time as much as of money.
senses.exampleCN: 父母投入的不只是钱，同样也是时间。
senses.why: The metaphor extends the agent noun beyond finance to anyone who accepts a cost now for a gain later.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻把施动名词带出金融领域，指任何现在承受代价以换取日后收益的人。

senses.title: Anyone bearing a cost for a later return
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：为日后回报承担代价的一方
senses.definition: any party that accepts an outlay of money, effort or risk in the expectation of a return
senses.definitionCN: 为期待回报而承受金钱、精力或风险支出的任何一方
senses.example: Every student is an investor in his own future.
senses.exampleCN: 每个学生都是自己未来的投资者。
senses.why: Stripped of finance, the word simply names the side that puts something in and waits.
senses.whyCN: 剥去金融外壳，这个词只指「投入某物并等待」的那一方。

intro.en: Investor is invest plus the Latin-derived agent suffix -or. Invest comes from Latin investire 'to clothe, surround'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: investor 由 invest 加源自拉丁语、表示施动者的后缀构成；invest 来自拉丁语 investire「穿衣、包围」。年代为约数。

items.en: Vestis meant 'garment'. Its deeper origin is uncertain and no reliable earlier root can be given.
items.cn: vestis 意为「衣服」。其更早来源不确定，无法给出可靠的更早词根。

items.en: In- 'in' plus vestire 'to clothe' produced investire, 'to clothe or surround', used of persons, offices and besieged towns.
items.cn: 表「进入」的前缀加 vestire「穿衣」构成 investire「穿衣、包围」，用于人、职位与被围的城镇。

items.en: English took the verb as invest, first for granting an office and for a siege, then from the seventeenth century for committing money.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词借为 invest，最初指授予职位与围城，十七世纪起指投入金钱。

items.en: The suffix -or continues Latin -or, which names the person who performs an action.
items.cn: 表示施动者的后缀承自拉丁语 -or，用来指执行某一动作的人。

items.en: Investor became a common label in the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries as joint-stock companies and stock markets spread.
items.cn: 随着股份公司与证券市场扩展，investor 在十八、十九世纪成为常用称呼。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first citation of investor is not settled, and the origin of vestis before Latin is unknown.
items.cn: 来源不确定：investor 的确切最早书证没有定论，vestis 在拉丁语之前的来源不明。

note.en: Group one holds the same investing family, where the grammatical role is the difference; group two holds people who supply or risk money.
note.cn: 第一组同属「投资」词族，差别在语法角色；第二组是提供资金或承担金钱风险的人。

entries.definition: The act of committing money; the person noun cannot be used for the act itself.
entries.definitionCN: 投入金钱的动作；指人的名词不能用来指这个动作。

entries.definition: Names the act or the money committed; it is not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 指行为或投入的金额；不是指人。

entries.definition: The activity as a continuing process; investor is the participant.
entries.definitionCN: 作为持续过程的活动；investor 是参与者。

entries.definition: A rare word for one who sells off assets; it is built on the same root with a prefix of separation.
entries.definitionCN: 指剥离资产者的罕用词；同根，带表分离的前缀。

entries.definition: A person who owns shares; every shareholder is an investor, but not every investor holds shares.
entries.definitionCN: 持有股份的人；每个股东都是投资者，但并非每个投资者都持有股份。

entries.definition: A person who manages or provides large sums of money, often as a profession.
entries.definitionCN: 管理或提供大额资金的人，常以此为其职业。

entries.definition: Someone who gives financial support to a person or venture, often informally.
entries.definitionCN: 向某人或某项目提供资金支持的人，常为较非正式的场合。

entries.definition: A person who buys assets hoping for a quick price gain, taking more risk than a typical investor.
entries.definitionCN: 为求价格快速上涨而买入资产的人，承担的风险高于一般的投资者。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real agent suffix, the real family and the real market phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的施动后缀、真实词族与真实市场搭配。

normal.en: Invest plus the person suffix: the one who puts money in.
normal.cn: invest 加指人的后缀：把钱投进去的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs invest, investor, investment, investable, reinvest.
normal.cn: 词族包括 invest、investor、investment、investable、reinvest。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market: institutional investor, retail investor, investor confidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场语境：机构投资者、散户投资者、投资者信心。

normal.en: A shareholder is one kind of investor, not the other way round.
normal.cn: 股东是投资者的一种，而不是反过来。

normal.en: The word can take organisations as well as people: a fund can be an investor.
normal.cn: 这个词既可指人也可指机构：一只基金也可以是投资者。

abstract.en: Picture a person buying a seed they will not eat for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人买下一粒多年后才会吃的种子。

abstract.en: Picture someone paying now for a key they cannot yet use.
abstract.cn: 想象有人现在付钱买一把还打不开任何门的钥匙。

abstract.en: Picture a person who lends a workshop its first tools and waits.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把第一批工具借给一间作坊，然后等待。

examples.en: The investor asked for a seat on the board.
examples.cn: 这位投资者要求获得一个董事会席位。

examples.en: Retail investors often buy after prices have already risen.
examples.cn: 散户投资者常在价格已经上涨之后才买入。

examples.en: A long-term investor can ignore a single bad quarter.
examples.cn: 长期投资者可以不在意单独一个糟糕的季度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「invest（投钱）＋表示『人』的后缀」——把钱投进去、等它长回来的人，就是投资者

root: invest（拉丁语 investire「穿衣、包围」，源自 vestis「衣服」）＋一个源自拉丁语、指执行动作者的施动后缀（拉丁语 -or）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one participant: someone puts value in and waits, and the same label then covers an institution, an early backer, a foreign source of capital, a shareholder, a supplier of funds, a giver of time and finally anyone who accepts a cost for a later return.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个参与者展开：某人把价值放进去然后等待；同一个称呼再指机构、早期出资人、海外资金来源、股东、资金提供方、付出时间的人，最后指任何为日后回报承受代价的一方。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at the table who puts money in and waits for the harvest.
core.cn: 核心意象：坐在桌边把钱放进去、等待收成的人。

branches.en: PERSON AND INSTITUTION: the same role is played by an individual and by a fund.
branches.cn: 个人与机构：同一个角色既由个人扮演，也由基金扮演。

branches.en: EARLY STAGE: the first backer of a young venture gets a name of his own.
branches.cn: 早期阶段：年轻项目的第一个出资人得到自己的名称。

branches.en: ACROSS BORDERS: capital from outside the country marks where the money began.
branches.cn: 跨国：来自国外的资本标出钱的起点。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP AND SUPPLY: buying shares and supplying capital are two results of the same act.
branches.cn: 所有权与供给：购买股份与提供资本是同一动作的两种结果。

branches.en: BEYOND MONEY: time and trust can be invested too, so the role outgrows finance.
branches.cn: 超出金钱：时间与信任也可以投入，因此这个角色超出金融领域。

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of clothing plus an agent suffix, and the suffix is the part that turns the act into a person.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表「穿衣」的拉丁动词加一个施动后缀构成，后缀正是把动作变成人的那部分。

latinIntro.en: Latin investire supplies the base; Latin -or supplies the ending that marks the doer.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 investire 提供词基；拉丁语 -or 提供标记执行者的词尾。

items.example: The prefix marks putting something in.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出「把东西放进去」。

items.example: The noun gives the clothing image.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词给出穿衣的意象。

items.example: The verb supplies invest.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供 invest。

items.example: They invest in land.
items.exampleCN: 他们投资土地。

items.example: The suffix names the doer.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀指执行者。

items.example: The investor signed the agreement.
items.exampleCN: 投资者签署了协议。

items.example: The investment took years to mature.
items.exampleCN: 这项投资用了多年才成熟。

items.example: The market is considered investable.
items.exampleCN: 该市场被视为可投资。

items.example: They reinvested the dividend.
items.exampleCN: 他们把股息再投资。

definition_zh: 资本主义；资本主导的经济制度
definition_en: an economic system in which private owners control capital and production for profit through markets
core_image: 一条街上并排开着私人店铺，每家门口都挂着自己写的价牌，顾客在门口来回比较
scene: 一条街上并排开着私人店铺，每家挂着自己写的价牌，顾客在门口来回比较。Supporters argue that capitalism rewards those who serve customers best.
sceneCN: 街上私人店铺各自标价，顾客在门口比较选择；句中的 capitalism 指「由私人资本与市场交换主导的经济制度」（第 1 个义项：生产资料主要为私人所有、以市场交易组织生产的经济制度）。图中可辨识物件：店招、手写价牌、收银台、橱窗、顾客。

pos.zh: 资本主义；资本主导的经济制度

senses.title: An economy run by private capital
senses.titleCN: 由私人资本运作的经济制度
senses.definition: an economic system in which private owners control the means of production and invest capital for profit
senses.definitionCN: 生产资料由私人所有者控制、并为获利而投入资本的经济制度
senses.example: Supporters argue that capitalism rewards those who serve customers best.
senses.exampleCN: 支持者主张，资本主义会奖励最会服务顾客的人。
senses.why: The word names a system by its central object: accumulated capital, held and reinvested by private owners.
senses.whyCN: 这个词以其核心对象命名一个制度：由私人持有并再投资的积累资本。

senses.title: Market competition as the mechanism
senses.titleCN: 作为运行机制的市场竞争
senses.definition: the arrangement in which prices, competition and profit coordinate what is produced
senses.definitionCN: 由价格、竞争与利润来协调生产内容的安排
senses.example: Cheap imports tested the capitalism of the old high street.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价进口商品考验了老商业街的市场竞争机制。
senses.why: A system is also its mechanism, so the word can point to competition rather than to ownership.
senses.whyCN: 制度同时也是其机制，因此这个词可以指竞争，而不指所有权。

senses.title: The ideology behind the system
senses.titleCN: 支撑该制度的意识形态
senses.definition: the set of beliefs that defend private property, profit and free exchange
senses.definitionCN: 为私有财产、利润与自由交换辩护的一套信念
senses.example: The pamphlet attacked capitalism as a creed rather than an economy.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子攻击资本主义是一种信条，而不只是一种经济。
senses.why: Defenders and critics alike turned the description of a system into a set of beliefs worth arguing about.
senses.whyCN: 无论辩护者还是批评者，都把对制度的描述变成了一套值得争论的信念。

senses.title: A historical phase of industry
senses.definition: a period or stage of economic history, such as industrial or finance capitalism
senses.definitionCN: 经济史上的某个时期或阶段，如工业资本主义或金融资本主义
senses.example: Historians date industrial capitalism from the early mills.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家把工业资本主义的起点定在早期的工厂。
senses.why: Once a system has a history, it is divided into phases, and the word carries those phase labels.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个制度有了历史，它就会被划分成阶段，这个词便承载这些阶段标签。

senses.title: A variety defined by who controls capital
senses.titleCN: 按资本控制者划分的形态
senses.definition: one of several forms distinguished by the relation between the state, finance and industry
senses.definitionCN: 依国家、金融与产业之间的关系而区分的若干形态之一
senses.example: State capitalism keeps ownership private but direction public.
senses.exampleCN: 国家资本主义让所有权保持私有，而方向由公共掌握。
senses.why: Comparisons within the system produce qualified forms, each stressing a different holder of capital.
senses.whyCN: 制度内部的比较产生了带限定的形态，每一种都强调不同的资本持有者。

senses.title: A critical label in Marxist writing
senses.titleCN: 马克思主义写作中的批判性标签
senses.definition: the term used in Marxist analysis for a system driven by the accumulation of capital and wage labour
senses.definitionCN: 马克思主义分析中用来指由资本积累与雇佣劳动驱动的制度的术语
senses.example: The course read capitalism through the lens of wage labour.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程从雇佣劳动的角度解读资本主义。
senses.why: A neutral description became a critical instrument when it was used to name the power behind the market.
senses.whyCN: 当这个词被用来指认市场背后的权力时，中性的描述就变成了批判的工具。

senses.title: Everyday market society
senses.definition: the ordinary, loosely used sense of a society in which most things are bought and sold
senses.definitionCN: 日常宽泛使用的意义：多数事物都被买卖的社会
senses.example: In everyday talk, capitalism simply means a world of shops and prices.
senses.exampleCN: 在日常言谈中，资本主义只意味着一个充满商店与价格的世界。
senses.why: Technical terms drift into common speech, where they lose precision and gain colour.
senses.whyCN: 术语会漂入日常语言，在那里失去精确性，却获得色彩。

senses.title: Any system organised around accumulated capital
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：围绕积累资本组织的任何体系
senses.definition: any arrangement in which accumulated resources are the main lever for organising production and exchange
senses.definitionCN: 以积累的资源作为组织生产与交换的主要杠杆的任何安排
senses.example: The author detected capitalism in the funding of the university itself.
senses.exampleCN: 作者在这所大学的自身经费结构中看出了资本主导的逻辑。
senses.why: At its widest the word describes a principle of organisation, not only a named historical economy.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽的意义上，这个词描述一种组织原则，而不只是一个有名字的历史经济形态。

intro.en: Capitalism joins capital, from Latin capitalis 'of the head' and, in medieval use, 'principal sum', with the Greek-derived suffix -ism. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: capitalism 由 capital 与一个源自希腊语、表示制度或学说的后缀构成；capital 来自拉丁语 capitalis「头部的」，中世纪用法中又指「本金」。年代为约数。

items.en: Caput meant 'head'. Its deeper origin is not established, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」。其更早来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

items.en: Capitalis meant 'of the head', and in medieval Latin capitale came to mean the principal sum of a loan, as opposed to interest.
items.cn: capitalis 意为「头部的」；在中世纪拉丁语中，capitale 转而指贷款的本金，与利息相对。

items.en: English capital acquired the sense of accumulated wealth used to produce more wealth in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: 英语 capital 在十六、十七世纪获得「用于生产更多财富的积累财富」这一意义。

items.en: The suffix reached English through Latin from Greek -ismos, and names systems, doctrines and movements.
items.cn: 这个后缀经拉丁语从希腊语 -ismos 进入英语，用来指制度、学说与运动。

items.en: Capitalism appears in the mid-nineteenth century and gained wide currency later in the century, especially in political economy and socialist criticism.
items.cn: capitalism 出现于十九世纪中叶，并在该世纪后期广泛通行，尤见于政治经济学与社会主义批评。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact first use of capitalism is disputed, and the deeper origin of caput is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定：capitalism 的最早使用存在争议，caput 的更早来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the words built on capital, which are regularly confused; group two holds other labels for economic orders.
note.cn: 第一组是由 capital 构成的词，常被混淆；第二组是其他经济秩序的标签。

entries.definition: The accumulated money and assets, or a chief city; the system is named after it but is not the stock itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指积累的资金与资产，也指首都；制度以它命名，但它本身不是制度。

entries.definition: A person who owns capital or supports the system; capitalism is the system, not the person.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有资本或支持该制度的人；capitalism 是制度，不是人。

entries.definition: Describes something as having the character of the system; it is an adjective, not the name of the system.
entries.definitionCN: 描述某物具有该制度的性质；是形容词，不是制度名称。

entries.definition: To convert into capital, to provide with capital, or to take advantage of something.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为资本、提供资本，或利用某事。

entries.definition: A term stressing private initiative and minimal state control rather than the ownership of capital.
entries.definitionCN: 强调私人创业与国家干预最少，而非资本所有权。

entries.definition: An economy coordinated by prices and trade; it does not specify who owns the capital.
entries.definitionCN: 由价格与贸易协调的经济；并不规定资本由谁所有。

entries.definition: A system in which production is socially or state owned, often contrasted directly with capitalism.
entries.definitionCN: 生产由社会或国家所有的制度，常与资本主义直接对照。

entries.definition: An earlier doctrine that measured national wealth in trade surpluses and bullion, not in industrial capital.
entries.definitionCN: 较早的学说，以贸易顺差与金银衡量国家财富，而非工业资本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real root 'head', the real nineteenth-century coinage and the real contrast with socialism.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「头」这一词根、真实的十九世纪造词，以及与社会主义的真实对照。

normal.en: Capital meant the principal sum, the 'head' of a loan, before it meant the wealth behind industry.
normal.cn: capital 先指贷款的本金，即债的「头」，后才指工业背后的财富。

normal.en: Capital plus the suffix of systems: the name of an order built on accumulated capital.
normal.cn: capital 加表示制度的后缀：一个建立在积累资本之上的秩序的名称。

normal.en: The family runs capital, capitalism, capitalist, capitalistic, capitalize.
normal.cn: 词族包括 capital、capitalism、capitalist、capitalistic、capitalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark its varieties: industrial capitalism, state capitalism, finance capitalism.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出其形态：工业资本主义、国家资本主义、金融资本主义。

normal.en: The word is defined against socialism, and the pair are usually taught together.
normal.cn: 这个词在与社会主义的对照中被定义，两者通常一起讲授。

abstract.en: Picture a street of shops where every price tag is written by a different hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上的商店，每张价签都出自不同人的手笔。

abstract.en: Picture a warehouse of goods that is constantly being enlarged by its own sales.
abstract.cn: 想象一座仓库，靠自己的销售不断变大。

abstract.en: Picture a game whose score is kept in money and whose players may join or leave freely.
abstract.cn: 想象一场以金钱记分的游戏，参与者可以自由加入或退出。

examples.en: The book traces capitalism from the first chartered companies.
examples.cn: 这本书从最早的特许公司写起，追溯资本主义的来历。

examples.en: Critics and defenders of capitalism rarely agree on its origins.
examples.cn: 资本主义的批评者与辩护者很少在其起源上达成一致。

examples.en: The region mixed capitalism with strong state direction.
examples.cn: 该地区把资本主义与强有力的国家引导混合在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「capital（资本）＋表示『主义』的后缀」——一切围绕资本转的制度，就是资本主义

root: capital（拉丁语 capitalis「头部的」，中世纪拉丁语 capitale 指本金）＋一个表示制度、学说或运动的后缀（经拉丁语来自希腊语 -ismos）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one principle: accumulated capital is the lever that organizes production, and that principle is then read as a system, a mechanism, a creed, a historical phase, a family of varieties, a critical label, an everyday word and finally any capital-centred arrangement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个原则展开：积累的资本是组织生产的杠杆；这个原则再被读成制度、机制、信条、历史阶段、形态家族、批判标签、日常用语，最后指任何以资本为中心的安排。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a street of private shops, each with its own price tag.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条私人店铺林立的街，每家都有自己的价签。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND MECHANISM: private ownership is the structure, and price competition is how it moves.
branches.cn: 制度与机制：私人所有权是结构，价格竞争是它运转的方式。

branches.en: CREED: a description of an order becomes a set of beliefs to defend or attack.
branches.cn: 信条：对一种秩序的描述，变成一套可供辩护或攻击的信念。

branches.en: HISTORY AND VARIETY: the system is divided into phases and into forms named after who holds the capital.
branches.cn: 历史与形态：这个制度被划分成阶段，也按资本持有者分成不同形态。

branches.en: CRITIQUE: the same term becomes an instrument for naming power behind the market.
branches.cn: 批判：同一个术语成为指认市场背后权力的工具。

branches.en: EVERYDAY AND GENERAL: the word drifts into common speech and then widens into any capital-centred principle.
branches.cn: 日常与泛化：这个词漂入日常语言，继而扩展为任何以资本为中心的原则。

intro.en: The word is a noun of wealth plus a suffix of systems, and both parts are productive in modern political vocabulary.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示财富的名词加一个表示制度的后缀构成，两部分在现代政治词汇中都很有构词力。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and capitalis supply capital; the suffix comes from Greek through Latin and names doctrines and orders.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 与 capitalis 提供 capital；后缀经拉丁语来自希腊语，用来指学说与秩序。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根指一笔债的「头」。

items.example: The adjective meant chief or principal.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词意为首要的、本金的。

items.example: The medieval noun named the principal of a loan.
items.exampleCN: 这个中世纪名词指贷款本金。

items.meaningCN: 用于生产更多财富的财富
items.example: Capital moved into the new mills.

items.example: The suffix names an order of things.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀为一种秩序命名。

items.meaningCN: 建立在资本之上的秩序
items.example: Capitalism spread with joint-stock trade.
items.exampleCN: 资本主义随股份制贸易扩展。

items.example: The capitalist financed the railway.
items.exampleCN: 这位资本家资助了铁路。

items.example: The rules had a capitalistic flavour.
items.exampleCN: 这些规则带有资本主义色彩。

items.meaning: to turn into or supply capital
items.example: The firm capitalized the new branch.
items.exampleCN: 公司为新分支提供了资本。

definition_zh: 资本家；资本主义者；资本主义的
definition_en: a person who owns or controls capital, or a supporter of capitalism; also the adjective meaning of that system
core_image: 一位工厂主站在厂房门口，手里拿着账本，身后是排队上工的工人
scene: 厂房门口，厂主拿着账本核对名单，身后的工人排成一列准备上工。The old capitalist sold the mill and moved his money into shipping.
sceneCN: 厂主在门口核对上工名单，身后工人排成一列；句中的 capitalist 指「拥有并支配资本的人」（第 1 个义项：私人资本的持有者与经营者）。图中可辨识物件：厂房门、账本、工人队列、上工牌、钱箱。

pos.zh: 资本家；资本主义的支持者

senses.title: An owner or controller of capital
senses.titleCN: 资本的拥有者或支配者
senses.definition: a person who owns or controls the money and assets used to run a business
senses.definitionCN: 拥有或支配用于经营企业的资金与资产的人
senses.example: The old capitalist sold the mill and moved his money into shipping.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老厂主卖掉了磨坊，把钱转投航运。
senses.why: The suffix marks a person attached to capital, so the core sense is the owner of the productive stock.
senses.whyCN: 后缀标出与资本相关联的人，因此核心义是生产性存量的所有者。

senses.title: A supporter of the system
senses.titleCN: 资本主义制度的支持者
senses.definition: a person who defends private ownership, profit and free markets as the best arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 主张私有财产、利润与自由市场是最佳安排的人
senses.example: He called himself a capitalist before he called himself a politician.
senses.exampleCN: 他先自称资本主义者，然后才自称政治家。
senses.why: When a system needs defenders, the person noun also names the adherent rather than only the owner.
senses.whyCN: 当一种制度需要辩护者时，指人的名词也用来指拥护者，而不只是所有者。

senses.title: A businessperson in a market economy
senses.definition: a person who runs or expands a business within a market economy
senses.definitionCN: 在市场经济中经营或扩张企业的人
senses.example: The town's capitalists built the first department store.
senses.exampleCN: 镇上的经营者建起了第一家百货商店。
senses.why: Ownership and management usually meet in one person, and the word shifts from owner to active businessman.
senses.whyCN: 所有权与经营通常集中在一人身上，这个词便从所有者转为活跃的经营者。

senses.title: A financier of ventures
senses.definition: a person who supplies money to ventures, especially in return for a share
senses.definitionCN: 向项目提供资金、尤以换取份额为条件的人
senses.example: A local capitalist backed the new railway line.
senses.exampleCN: 一位本地出资人资助了那条新铁路。
senses.why: Capital must be put somewhere, and the person who supplies it to a project is called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 资本总得投到某处，而把资本提供给项目的人也被这样称呼。

senses.title: A class label in Marxist analysis
senses.titleCN: 马克思主义分析中的阶级标签
senses.definition: the term used in Marxist analysis for the class that owns the means of production
senses.definitionCN: 马克思主义分析中用来指拥有生产资料的那个阶级的术语
senses.example: The pamphlet addressed the capitalist as a class, not a man.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子把资本家当作一个阶级而非一个人来论述。
senses.why: Political economy turned a personal noun into a class noun, so the word can name a social position.
senses.whyCN: 政治经济学把指个人的名词变成指阶级的名词，因此这个词可以指一种社会位置。

senses.title: A venture capitalist
senses.definition: a person or firm that invests in young companies in exchange for equity, accepting high risk
senses.definitionCN: 以换取股权的方式投资年轻公司、承担高风险的个人或机构
senses.example: A venture capitalist took a third of the young firm.
senses.exampleCN: 一位风险投资人拿走了这家年轻公司的三分之一。
senses.why: Fixed phrases divide the role by stage and risk, and the venture variety became a standard term.
senses.whyCN: 固定搭配按阶段与风险划分角色，风险投资这一类型成为标准说法。

senses.title: Of the capitalist system
senses.titleCN: 资本主义制度的（形容词义）
senses.definition: describing an economy, society or rule that has the character of capitalism
senses.definitionCN: 形容具有资本主义性质的经济、社会或规则
senses.example: The country kept a capitalist economy under a strong state.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家在强国家之下保留了资本主义经济。
senses.why: English often uses the same form as noun and adjective, so the person noun doubles as a description of the system.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让名词与形容词同形，于是指人的名词也兼作对制度的描述。

senses.title: Anyone who turns resources into seeking profit
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把资源转为逐利资本的人
senses.definition: any person who converts available resources into capital aimed at profit
senses.definitionCN: 把可用资源转化为以获利为目标的资本的任何人
senses.example: Every small trader is a capitalist in miniature.
senses.exampleCN: 每个小商贩都是微缩版的资本家。
senses.why: At its widest the word describes a role in an economy, not a particular historical class.
senses.whyCN: 在最宽的意义上，这个词描述经济中的一种角色，而不是某个特定历史阶级。

intro.en: Capitalist joins capital, from Latin capitalis 'of the head' and medieval capitale 'principal sum', with the Greek-derived suffix -ist. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: capitalist 由 capital 与一个源自希腊语、表示人的后缀构成；capital 来自拉丁语 capitalis「头部的」及中世纪拉丁语 capitale「本金」。年代为约数。

items.en: Caput meant 'head'. Its deeper origin is not established, and proposed Indo-European roots are reconstructions.
items.cn: caput 意为「头」。其更早来源未得到证明，所提出的印欧词根均属重构形式。

items.en: In medieval Latin capitale meant the principal sum of a debt, the 'head' from which interest grew.
items.cn: 在中世纪拉丁语中，capitale 指债务的本金，即生出利息的那个「头」。

items.en: By the seventeenth century English capital meant accumulated wealth used to produce more wealth.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，英语 capital 已指用于生产更多财富的积累财富。

items.en: The suffix came through Latin from Greek -istēs and names a person who practices or supports something.
items.cn: 这个后缀经拉丁语来自希腊语 -istēs，用来指从事或支持某事的人。

items.en: Capitalist first named a person with capital in the late eighteenth century, and by the mid-nineteenth it also named a supporter of the system and a class in socialist analysis.
items.cn: capitalist 在十八世纪晚期先指拥有资本的人，到十九世纪中叶又指制度支持者，并在社会主义分析中指一个阶级。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first date of the class sense is disputed, and the deeper origin of caput is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：阶级义的首见年代存在争议，caput 的更早来源属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds the capital family, where noun and adjective forms are easy to mix; group two holds other names for people with money or business power.
note.cn: 第一组是 capital 词族，名词与形容词形式容易混淆；第二组是其他指有钱或有商业权力者的名称。

entries.definition: The money and assets themselves, or a chief city; a capitalist is the person who holds them.
entries.definitionCN: 指资金与资产本身，也指首都；capitalist 指持有它们的人。

entries.definition: The economic order, not a person; the two words differ in suffix and in what they can be the subject of.
entries.definitionCN: 指经济秩序，不是指人；两个词的差别在后缀，也在能充当什么主语。

entries.definition: Describes a thing or system as having that character; it does not name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 描述事物或制度具有那种性质；不指人。

entries.definition: To provide with capital, to convert into capital, or to exploit an opportunity.
entries.definitionCN: 提供资本、使成为资本，或利用机会。

entries.definition: A person who commits money expecting a return; a capitalist owns the productive stock itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为期待回报而投入资金的人；资本家则拥有生产性存量本身。

entries.definition: A person who manages or supplies large sums, often professionally; the word stresses finance rather than ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 管理或提供大额资金的人，常为职业；强调金融而非所有权。

entries.definition: A person who starts and runs a business, taking the risk; capitalists may supply the money instead.
entries.definitionCN: 创办并经营企业、承担风险的人；资本家可能只是提供资金的一方。

entries.definition: A person who owns or controls large industrial enterprises; it is narrower than capitalist.
entries.definitionCN: 拥有或控制大型工业企业的人；比 capitalist 更窄。

entries.definition: A member of the propertied middle class in Marxist and historical usage; it is a class position, not an economic role.
entries.definitionCN: 马克思主义与历史用法中有产的中产阶级成员；是阶级位置，不是经济角色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real root, the real suffix and the real distinction from the system's name.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实词根、真实后缀，以及它与制度名称的真实区别。

normal.en: Capital plus the suffix for a person: the one who owns the productive stock.
normal.cn: capital 加指人的后缀：拥有生产性存量的人。

normal.en: The family runs capital, capitalism, capitalist, capitalistic, capitalize.
normal.cn: 词族包括 capital、capitalism、capitalist、capitalistic、capitalize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the role: venture capitalist, industrial capitalist, capitalist class.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出角色：风险投资人、工业资本家、资本家阶级。

normal.en: Capitalism is the system; a capitalist is a person or, as an adjective, a kind of system.
normal.cn: 资本主义是制度；capitalist 是人，作形容词时指某种制度。

normal.en: An investor may hold shares; a capitalist owns the capital that stands behind them.
normal.cn: 投资者可能持有股份；资本家拥有股份背后的资本。

abstract.en: Picture a man at a factory gate with an account book in one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在工厂门口，一手拿着账本。

abstract.en: Picture a purse large enough that other people's work depends on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只大到别人的工作都要依赖它的钱袋。

abstract.en: Picture a person who buys a field not to stand in but to rent out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人买下一块地，不是为了站进去，而是为了租出去。

examples.en: The capitalist kept the profits and paid the workers a fixed wage.
examples.cn: 资本家留下利润，付给工人固定工资。

examples.en: She described herself as a capitalist who believed in competition.
examples.cn: 她称自己是相信竞争的资本主义者。

examples.en: The venture capitalist wanted a share of the company.
examples.cn: 这位风险投资人想要公司的一部分股份。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「capital（资本）＋表示『人』的后缀」——手里握着资本的人，就是资本家

root: capital（拉丁语 capitalis「头部的」，中世纪拉丁语 capitale 指本金）＋一个表示人的后缀（经拉丁语来自希腊语 -istēs，指从事或支持某事的人）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one holder: someone owns the productive stock, and that role is then read as a defender of the system, a business operator, a supplier of funds, a class position, a venture specialist, an adjective for the system and finally any converter of resources into profit-seeking capital.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个持有者展开：某人拥有生产性存量；这个角色再被读成制度的辩护者、经营企业者、资金提供者、阶级位置、风险投资专才、制度的形容词，最后指任何把资源转为逐利资本的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at the factory gate holding the account book.
core.cn: 核心意象：站在工厂门口、手握账本的人。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: holding the stock and supplying money to ventures are two faces of the same owner.
branches.cn: 所有权：持有存量与向项目提供资金，是同一个所有者的两面。

branches.en: ADHERENCE: defending the system turns an owner into a believer.
branches.cn: 拥护：为制度辩护，使所有者变成信从者。

branches.en: OPERATION: ownership in action looks like running a business.
branches.cn: 经营：所有权在行动中看起来就是经营企业。

branches.en: POSITION AND SPECIALITY: analysis turns the person into a class, and finance into a venture role.
branches.cn: 位置与专长：分析把人变成阶级，金融则把它变成一种风险投资角色。

branches.en: DESCRIPTION: the same form serves as an adjective, and at its widest it names anyone who turns resources into capital.
branches.cn: 描述：同一形式兼作形容词，最宽时指任何把资源转为资本的人。

intro.en: The word is a noun of wealth plus a suffix for a person, and the same base also builds the system's name and its adjective.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个表示财富的名词加一个指人的后缀构成，同一词基还构成制度名称及其形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput and capitale supply capital; the suffix came from Greek through Latin and marks an adherent or practitioner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput 与 capitale 提供 capital；后缀经拉丁语来自希腊语，标记拥护者或从业者。

items.exampleCN: 这个词根指债务的「头」。

items.example: The principal was the head of the loan.
items.exampleCN: 本金就是贷款的头。

items.example: Capital financed the new works.
items.exampleCN: 资本为新工程提供资金。

items.example: The suffix marks the adherent.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标记拥护者。

items.example: The capitalist expanded the works.
items.exampleCN: 这位资本家扩建了工厂。

items.meaningCN: 建立在资本之上的秩序
items.example: Capitalism spread with industry.
items.exampleCN: 资本主义随工业扩展。

items.example: The reform had a capitalistic aim.
items.exampleCN: 这项改革带有资本主义目的。

items.meaning: to supply or convert into capital
items.meaningCN: 提供资本或使成为资本
items.example: They capitalized the new firm.

items.example: The capitalization of the firm doubled.
items.exampleCN: 该公司的总市值翻了一倍。
